AU.text:
In Australia the New Year falls in summer, so the party moves outdoors: fireworks, concerts and exhibitions, many of them at beaches. Some head to a party with music, a boat cruise, a city park or the beach; others gather at home for a barbecue. At midnight the fireworks go up and glasses of champagne or wine are raised. Big cities stage two shows: an early family one in the evening and the main one at midnight. 31 December is not a public holiday; 1 January is a day off in every state and territory.

Sydney fires two shows, at 9 pm and at midnight, from the Harbour Bridge, the Opera House and barges on the harbour. The 9 pm show, Calling Country, celebrates sky, land and sea and is created by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander artists. In 2025 the City of Sydney expected more than a million people on the harbour foreshore.

traditions.title: Beach, park or barbecue
traditions.text: Here the New Year comes in midsummer: people see it in on the beach, in a city park, on a boat or at a home barbecue. At midnight, glasses of champagne or wine go up.

traditions.title: Two shows in one night
traditions.text: Big cities stage an early family show and the main one at midnight. In 2025 the early one was at 9 pm in Sydney and Adelaide and at 9:30 pm in Melbourne and Hobart.

traditions.title: A spot on Sydney Harbour
traditions.text: The harbour has 49 vantage points, and parks and headlands are free to watch from. In 2025 the top spots, such as the Opera House Forecourt, took free registered tickets.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Australia: Sydney Harbour | Time2Fest
meta.description: Australia greets 2027 in summer, and Sydney fires two shows from the Harbour Bridge, Opera House and barges, at 9 pm and midnight. Sydney midnight is 13:00 UTC.

BR.text:
Brazil welcomes the New Year — Réveillon — in white. The custom began with Candomblé followers who, in the 1970s, came to Copacabana beach in white with gifts for Iemanjá, the water goddess; since then white clothes and flowers set out to sea have spread across the country. At midnight people on the coast jump seven waves, making a wish on each.

In Rio de Janeiro the party is on Copacabana: the city estimates more than 2.6 million people came to greet 2026. At midnight fireworks fired from 19 barges for 12 minutes, 1,200 drones rose into the sky, and three stages played on the beach.

traditions.title: All in white
traditions.text: People come to the beach in new white clothes. The custom goes back to Candomblé followers who greeted the New Year on Copacabana in white in the 1970s.

traditions.title: Gifts for Iemanjá
traditions.text: Iemanjá is a water goddess in Candomblé and Umbanda. People bring her flowers or small boats with gifts and push them out to sea — non-believers too.

traditions.title: Seven waves
traditions.text: At midnight people jump seven waves, making a wish on each: seven is a sacred number in Umbanda.

meta.title: Réveillon 2027 in Brazil: Copacabana at Midnight | Time2Fest
meta.description: Millions in white greet 2027 on Copacabana in Rio, Brazil: fireworks over the ocean, seven waves for luck and flowers for Iemanjá. Rio’s midnight is 03:00 UTC.

FR.text:
In France the last night of the year is called the Saint-Sylvestre, and it is spent over a festive dinner — the réveillon. It can be a quiet meal with family and friends or a party with dancing; on the table are foie gras, oysters and champagne, and people stay up until midnight. At 20:00 on 31 December the president addresses the French on television, reviewing the year and offering wishes — no president has missed it since 1958. At midnight some kiss under the mistletoe, a folk custom for luck.

In Paris the main party is on the Champs-Élysées: since 2014 the city has staged a free family show there. A giant video mapping is projected onto the Arc de Triomphe, and at midnight fireworks burst above it. According to the Interior Ministry, more than a million people greeted 2026 there.

traditions.title: The réveillon
traditions.text: A festive dinner on 31 December with foie gras, oysters and champagne — with family and friends or at a party with dancing. People stay up until midnight.

traditions.title: A kiss under the mistletoe
traditions.text: As midnight strikes, some kiss under a ball of mistletoe for a good year. It is a folk custom, said to have come from England in the 18th century.

traditions.title: Champs-Élysées show
traditions.text: A video mapping lights up the Arc de Triomphe, then fireworks burst above it at midnight. Entry is free; more than a million people greeted 2026 here.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in France: Champs-Élysées Show | Time2Fest
meta.description: France greets 2027 with a réveillon dinner, a kiss under the mistletoe and fireworks over the Arc de Triomphe in Paris. Midnight in France is 23:00 UTC.

GB.text:
In the United Kingdom midnight arrives with the chimes of Big Ben: in England the main celebration is in central London, with big events in Manchester, Liverpool and Birmingham too. At midnight people sing Auld Lang Syne, set to Robert Burns's 1788 poem; in Scotland they form a circle and cross arms for the last verse. There New Year's Eve is Hogmanay: right after midnight people go first-footing with coal, shortbread or whisky, as the first visitor brings the house its luck for the year. 1 January is a holiday across the country, and in Scotland so is the 2nd.

In London the countdown runs to the bongs of Big Ben. Fireworks have lit the Thames by the London Eye since 2004. For 2026, City Hall says about 100,000 ticketholders lined the banks as more than 12,000 fireworks burned for 12 minutes.

traditions.title: Auld Lang Syne
traditions.text: At midnight people sing the old song set to Robert Burns's 1788 poem. In Scotland they stand in a circle and cross arms at the last verse.

traditions.title: First-footing at Hogmanay
traditions.text: In Scotland, right after midnight, people visit friends and neighbours with coal, shortbread or whisky. The first visitor is said to set the household's luck for the year.

traditions.title: Big Ben and Thames fireworks
traditions.text: London counts down to the bongs of Big Ben, then fireworks burst around the London Eye, as every year since 2004. For 2026, City Hall says more than 12,000 fireworks lit the sky for 12 minutes.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in the United Kingdom: London | Time2Fest
meta.description: The United Kingdom greets 2027 as Big Ben chimes over London, fireworks light the Thames and Scots go first-footing for Hogmanay. UK midnight is 00:00 UTC.

JP.text:
In Japan the New Year is a quiet family holiday rather than a street party. From about 29 December to 3 January most people are off, the streets empty and temples and shrines fill up. 31 December is Ōmisoka: in the evening people eat toshikoshi soba buckwheat noodles, and at midnight Buddhist temples ring their bell 108 times; at many, the last strike falls in the new year.

On 1 January families eat osechi at home — festive dishes in stacked boxes, each with a wish for the year — and in the first days of January they visit a shrine for a charm and a fortune. In Tokyo the biggest crowds go to Meiji Jingu and Sensō-ji, while the Shibuya street countdown has been cancelled in recent years.

traditions.title: Joya no Kane
traditions.text: Buddhist temples ring their bell 108 times: at many, 107 strikes fall in the old year and the last one in the new. Some temples let visitors strike the bell too.

traditions.title: Toshikoshi soba
traditions.text: On the evening of 31 December people eat buckwheat soba noodles. The long noodles stand for a long life, and because they break easily they cut off the hardships of the old year.

traditions.title: Hatsumōde
traditions.text: The first shrine visit of the year, usually on 1–3 January; some go right after midnight. People buy an omamori charm and draw an omikuji fortune.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Japan: 108 Bells at Midnight | Time2Fest
meta.description: In Tokyo, temple bells ring 108 times as 2027 begins; families eat toshikoshi soba and visit a shrine. Midnight in Japan falls at 15:00 UTC on 31 December.

NZ.text:
New Zealand is among the first countries to see the New Year — in midsummer, on daylight time UTC+13, and on the Chatham Islands 45 minutes earlier still. For many New Zealanders the holidays mean summer, the beach and camping: historian Richard Wolfe explains that leaving town over Christmas and January became part of local culture back in the 1950s.

In Auckland a laser show lights the 328-metre Sky Tower from 9 pm, and at midnight five minutes of fireworks fire from three levels of the tower. The Harbour Bridge glows to music, and crowds gather on the waterfront and on Mt Eden, North Head and Mt Victoria.

traditions.title: Summer by the sea
traditions.text: Here the New Year falls in summer: many people leave town for beaches and campsites — a habit that took shape back in the 1950s.

traditions.title: Sky Tower fireworks
traditions.text: At midnight five minutes of fireworks fire from three levels of the 328-metre tower; from 9 pm it carries a laser and projection show.

traditions.title: Bridge and hilltops
traditions.text: The Harbour Bridge glows to music, and the fireworks are best seen from the waterfront and Mt Eden, North Head and Mt Victoria. Watching is free.

meta.title: New Year in Auckland, New Zealand: Sky Tower | Time2Fest
meta.description: Auckland, New Zealand, is among the first big cities to greet 2027: five minutes of fireworks from the Sky Tower and a lit Harbour Bridge. Midnight: 11:00 UTC.

US.text:
In the United States the New Year is welcomed in front of the TV and in town squares, counting down with New Year’s Rockin’ Eve, on air since 1973. At midnight people sing Auld Lang Syne, a habit set by Guy Lombardo’s orchestra, which played it on the radio from 1929. Many cities have their own symbol: Atlanta drops a peach, Miami raises a Big Orange and fireworks light up the Las Vegas Strip. 1 January is a federal holiday: in the South people eat black-eyed peas and collard greens for luck, and Pasadena holds the Rose Parade.

In New York, Times Square has hosted the party since 1904 and the ball has dropped here since 1907. Today a crystal ball 12.5 feet wide glides 90 feet down its mast in 60 seconds. Entry is free; for 2026 the NYPD expected about a million people.

traditions.title: Auld Lang Syne at midnight
traditions.text: When midnight comes, everyone sings it together. Guy Lombardo’s orchestra made it the sound of New Year’s in North America, playing it on air from New York from 1929.

traditions.title: The ball drop on TV
traditions.text: The country watches New Year’s Rockin’ Eve or the free webcast from Times Square. A minute before midnight the Mayor of New York presses a crystal button and the ball slowly descends its mast.

traditions.title: Lucky food on 1 January
traditions.text: In the South the first day of the year means black-eyed peas, red beans and rice and collard greens, all for luck. Then come the Rose Parade in Pasadena and college football bowl games.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in the United States: New York | Time2Fest
meta.description: The United States greets 2027 in New York: the Times Square ball drops for a minute and wish confetti rains from rooftops. Midnight is 00:00 local, 05:00 UTC.

UA.text:
In Ukraine the New Year is a family holiday around the table: olivier salad, herring under a fur coat, kholodets, tangerines and champagne — dishes that took root back in Soviet times. In the last minutes of the year the president addresses the nation on TV (in 2025 the address aired at 23:40), and glasses are raised and wishes made as the clock strikes midnight.

Under martial law fireworks and firecrackers are banned and Kyiv has a curfew from 00:00 to 05:00, so people celebrate at home. The country’s main tree stands on Sofiivska Square. Since Christmas moved to 25 December in 2023, the holidays run from Christmas Eve to 6 January, and in January Chernivtsi holds its Malanka parade.

traditions.title: The president’s address
traditions.text: In the last minutes of the year the president gives a New Year address; in 2025 it aired at 23:40. Then come the midnight chimes and a glass of champagne.

traditions.title: The festive table
traditions.text: The family gathers round a table of olivier salad, herring under a fur coat, kholodets and tangerines — dishes that took root back in Soviet times.

traditions.title: The tree on Sofiivska Square
traditions.text: The country’s main tree stands on Sofiivska Square in Kyiv; in 2025 it was decorated after the frescoes of St Sophia’s Cathedral, with no mass events. Fireworks and firecrackers are banned; party poppers and sparklers are allowed.

meta.title: New Year in Ukraine: Kyiv Midnight Countdown | Time2Fest
meta.description: Ukraine welcomes 2027 at midnight Kyiv time, 22:00 UTC: a festive family table, the countdown of the last seconds at home and the main tree on Sofiivska Square.

ES.text:
In Spain the New Year arrives with grapes: at midnight people eat twelve of them to the twelve chimes of the clock, one per chime, for luck and prosperity. The custom is first recorded in 1895, and by 1903 it was known across the country. Television has shown the chimes since 1962; the first minute of 2026 drew more than 5.8 million viewers on La 1. After the grapes comes a glass of cava, sometimes with a gold ring at the bottom, drunk in one go. And for luck in love, folk belief says to wear red underwear.

In Madrid the countdown happens in Puerta del Sol: the chimes ring from the clock on the Royal House of the Post Office, inaugurated in 1866, and about half a minute before midnight a ball drops as the cue to get ready. To welcome 2025, Time Out reported, up to 15,000 people were let into the square.

traditions.title: Twelve grapes
traditions.text: At midnight people eat one grape for each of the twelve chimes, one for every month's luck. To keep up, supermarkets sell cans of seedless grapes.

traditions.title: Cava with a gold ring
traditions.text: After the grapes comes a glass of cava: a gold ring or coin goes in for prosperity, a strawberry for love. The glass is finished in one go.

traditions.title: Red underwear, right foot
traditions.text: Folk belief says red underwear on New Year's Eve attracts love. And people step into the new year right foot first.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Spain: Madrid | Time2Fest
meta.description: Spain greets 2027 with twelve grapes, one per chime of the Puerta del Sol clock in Madrid, then cava and red underwear for luck. Madrid midnight is 23:00 UTC.

RO.text:
Romania sees in the New Year with carols and masked players. On New Year's Eve and New Year's Day carolers go round with Plugușorul, the 'little plough' carol, and in villages they sometimes carry a real plough from house to house. On the evening of 31 December villagers also bring out the buhai, a barrel covered with sheepskin that bellows like a bull. On 1 January children and young people come with the sorcova, a stick decked with flowers and ribbons, wishing health and luck. In Moldavia and Muntenia people play the Goat, which dies and comes back to life like the old year and the new. Grapes and figs go on the table for plenty. 1 and 2 January are holidays.

Bucharest's main open-air party moves every year: for 2025 it was in Titan Park with fireworks and 320 drones, for 2026 a free concert in Piața Alba Iulia by the Christmas market, with fireworks at midnight. The venue for 2027 has not been announced yet.

traditions.title: Plugușorul
traditions.text: On New Year's Eve and New Year's Day carolers go from house to house singing Plugușorul, the 'little plough' carol. In villages they sometimes carry a real plough with them.

traditions.title: Sorcova
traditions.text: On 1 January, St Basil's day, children and young people come with the sorcova, a stick decked with flowers, coloured paper and ribbons. They tap their hosts lightly and wish them health and plenty, and get sweets or money in thanks.

traditions.title: The Goat and the Bear
traditions.text: On New Year's Day in Moldavia and Muntenia people play the Goat, which dies and comes back to life like the old year and the new. In Moldavia young men in bearskins dance to drums, and in Maramureș masked players with bells and whips drive away evil spirits.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Romania: Bucharest | Time2Fest
meta.description: Romania greets 2027 with the Plugușor carol, buhai drums and goat and bear dances, plus a free open-air concert in Bucharest. Midnight: 00:00 local, 22:00 UTC.

DE.text:
Germany welcomes the New Year — Silvester — with parties, a glass of Sekt and the wish «Guten Rutsch!». Since 1972 German TV has shown the British sketch Dinner for One on New Year's Eve. People tell fortunes by pouring melted tin or wax into cold water: lead sets have not been sold in the EU since 2018. They give lucky charms — pigs, clover, ladybugs and horseshoes — and eat jam-filled doughnuts and a marzipan pig. Almost everyone sets off fireworks, allowed from 18:00 on 31 December to 07:00 on 1 January.

Berlin's biggest public fireworks are at the Brandenburg Gate. To welcome 2026, the state of Berlin held a free party there, Yeah26, with DJs and fireworks at midnight; the Senate announced about 20,000 free tickets. For 2027 a party at the Gate has been announced again. Private fireworks are banned there, as in several districts of the city.

traditions.title: Dinner for One
traditions.text: Since 1972 German TV has shown this British sketch, recorded in Hamburg in 1963, every New Year's Eve. Its line «Same procedure as every year» is a German catchphrase.

traditions.title: Lucky charms and doughnuts
traditions.text: For luck, people give little pigs, clover, ladybugs and horseshoes. With the Sekt come jam-filled doughnuts and a marzipan pig.

traditions.title: Fireworks and the Gate
traditions.text: Rockets and firecrackers may go up from 18:00 on 31 December to 07:00 on 1 January. In Berlin a free party with DJs and fireworks at the Brandenburg Gate has been announced again for 2027.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Germany: Berlin | Time2Fest
meta.description: Germany greets 2027 with Sekt, tin pouring and Dinner for One, while Berlin gathers at the Brandenburg Gate for fireworks. Midnight: 00:00 local, 23:00 UTC.

GR.text:
In Greece New Year's Eve is spent at home with family and the vasilopita, St Basil's pie with a coin baked inside. Around midnight the head of the house crosses the pie with a knife and cuts the slices: the first for God, the Virgin Mary and the house, then one for everyone from eldest to youngest. Whoever finds the coin is said to be lucky all year. In the evening people play cards for small stakes, and children go from door to door singing kalanda carols to a triangle. Around midnight or on 1 January a pomegranate is smashed on the doorstep: the more seeds scatter, the more luck. Children get their presents from St Basil on 1 January, his feast day.

Last year Athens saw in midnight at Syntagma Square: free entry, live music, a drone show before midnight, the largest ever in Attica, and at midnight silent fireworks, out of respect for animals and people sensitive to noise.

traditions.title: Vasilopita with a coin
traditions.text: Around midnight the head of the house crosses the pie with a knife and cuts slices, first for God and the house, then for everyone from eldest to youngest. Whoever gets the coin is said to be lucky all year.

traditions.title: A pomegranate on the doorstep
traditions.text: Around midnight or on 1 January a pomegranate is smashed on the doorstep: the more seeds scatter, the more luck. The first to step in, right foot first, is someone lucky, often a child.

traditions.title: Silent fireworks at Syntagma
traditions.text: Last year the City of Athens held a free countdown at Syntagma Square with a drone show before midnight. At midnight came silent fireworks, out of respect for animals and people sensitive to noise.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Greece: Athens | Time2Fest
meta.description: Greece greets 2027 with coin-filled vasilopita, a smashed pomegranate and kalanda carols; Athens counts down at Syntagma Square. Athens midnight: 22:00 UTC.

IT.text:
In Italy New Year's Eve is the Night of Saint Sylvester. People spend it with family or friends: at home over a big dinner, or in a square with concerts. On the table are cotechino or zampone with lentils: the round seeds look like coins and promise prosperity. At 20:30 the country tunes in to the President's address on radio and TV. The last ten seconds before midnight are counted out loud, then glasses of spumante go up and everyone exchanges wishes. And for luck people wear red underwear: wearing red on this night, tradition says, goes back to ancient Rome.

In Rome the city marked the arrival of 2026 at the Circus Maximus: a free concert from 21:00, and at midnight the mayor raised a glass with everyone right on stage. According to the city, more than 70,000 people came. Firecrackers and amateur fireworks are banned in the city over the holidays.

traditions.title: Lentils with cotechino
traditions.text: The New Year's Eve dinner brings cotechino or zampone with lentils. The round seeds look like coins, for a generous year ahead.

traditions.title: Red underwear
traditions.text: Tradition says red was worn on this night back in ancient Rome; today it is underwear. Some put it on backwards and turn it round after midnight.

traditions.title: Countdown and spumante
traditions.text: The last ten seconds before midnight are counted out loud, then glasses of spumante go up. At midnight fireworks light up skies across the country.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Italy: Rome | Time2Fest
meta.description: Italy greets 2027 with lentils, red underwear and spumante, while Rome heads to a free concert at the Circus Maximus. Roman countdown ends at 23:00 UTC.

HK.text:
In Hong Kong 1 January is a public holiday, but only for one day. The year's big festival is Lunar New Year: three days off, a family reunion dinner on the eve, visits to relatives and red envelopes of money. In 2027 it falls on 6 February, and the celebrations last until the Lantern Festival on the fifteenth day. Still, the night of 31 December is shared too, with a countdown by Victoria Harbour and in Lan Kwai Fong.

To welcome 2025, fireworks fired from barges and rooftops lit the harbour for 12 minutes, a countdown clock glowed on the Convention and Exhibition Centre facade, and over 400,000 people watched, the government said. A year later the fireworks were cancelled out of respect for those affected by the Tai Po fire. For 2027 the Tourism Board has announced their return on a larger scale than ever.

traditions.title: Lunar New Year comes first
traditions.text: The year's biggest festival is Lunar New Year, on 6 February in 2027: families gather for a reunion dinner on the eve, visit relatives and hand out red envelopes of money. 1 January is just a one-day holiday.

traditions.title: Count down with the city
traditions.text: The last seconds are counted on a giant clock on the Convention and Exhibition Centre facade, and to welcome 2026 a live concert played in Central. Another favourite countdown spot is Lan Kwai Fong.

traditions.title: Victoria Harbour fireworks
traditions.text: To welcome 2025, fireworks from barges and rooftops lit the harbour for 12 minutes. For 2027 the Tourism Board has announced their return on a larger scale than ever.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Hong Kong | Time2Fest
meta.description: Hong Kong greets 2027 with a countdown by Victoria Harbour, Lunar New Year in February and the announced return of its harbour fireworks. Midnight: 16:00 UTC.

KR.text:
South Korea has 1 January off, but the main holiday here is Seollal, the lunar New Year, which falls on 7 February in 2027. Still, New Year's Eve on 31 December is celebrated too, with gatherings in most cities. On the morning of 1 January families and friends head to the east coast, the sea or the mountains: a wish made at the year's first sunrise is believed to bring luck. Tteokguk, a soup of sliced rice cakes, is eaten above all at Seollal; a bowl was once said to add a year to your age. Since June 2023, when age began to be counted from the birthday, that is only a saying.

In Seoul the Bosingak Pavilion bell rings out at midnight: eleven selected citizens strike it 33 times. The ceremony has been held since 1953; KBS expects up to 100,000 people, and it is shown live.

traditions.title: A wish at the first sunrise
traditions.text: On the morning of 1 January people head to the east coast, the sea or the mountains to make a wish at the first sunrise. Those who skip the early trip make theirs at the year's last sunset on 31 December.

traditions.title: Tteokguk, a year older
traditions.text: This soup of sliced rice cakes is eaten above all at Seollal, the lunar New Year. A bowl was believed to add a year, though since 2023 age is counted from the birthday.

traditions.title: Bosingak bell, 33 strikes
traditions.text: At midnight in central Seoul eleven selected citizens strike the Bosingak bell 33 times, a number from Buddhist tradition. The ceremony is shown live.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in South Korea: Seoul | Time2Fest
meta.description: South Korea greets 2027 in Seoul as the Bosingak bell rings 33 times; families eat tteokguk and chase the first sunrise on the east coast. Midnight: 15:00 UTC.

TW.text:
In Taiwan 1 January is a public holiday, though the biggest celebration of the year is Lunar New Year. The night is welcomed with open-air concerts and fireworks: Taichung, Kaohsiung and New Taipei hold their own countdowns. In the morning many head to the mountains or the east coast for the first sunrise of the year: last time the earliest sun was due at 6:03am on a peak above 3,000 m in Hualien County. Last time on Alishan the dawn was greeted with classical music, and on the morning of 1 January the flag is raised in front of the Presidential Office in Taipei.

In Taipei the main party is a concert on the plaza by City Hall, where tens of thousands gather. At midnight fireworks burst from the 508-metre Taipei 101 tower: the first show lit its opening night in 2004, and last time it lasted six minutes. Hundreds of thousands watch it in Xinyi District.

traditions.title: First sunrise of the year
traditions.text: On the morning of 1 January people head to the mountains or the east coast to catch the year's first sun. Last time on Alishan the dawn was greeted with a classical music concert.

traditions.title: Flag-raising in Taipei
traditions.text: On the morning of 1 January the flag is raised in front of the Presidential Office in Taipei. In 2025 the ceremony was followed by the president's New Year address, and guests received red envelopes.

traditions.title: Taipei 101 fireworks
traditions.text: At midnight fireworks burst straight from the Taipei 101 skyscraper, while a concert on the City Hall plaza counts down to them. Last time the show lasted six minutes.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Taiwan: Taipei | Time2Fest
meta.description: Taipei, Taiwan welcomes 2027 with a City Hall concert and fireworks from Taipei 101, then many climb peaks for the first sunrise. Local midnight is 16:00 UTC.

PH.text:
The Philippines welcomes the New Year with Media Noche, a midnight feast of family and friends. On the table: pancit, long noodles for a long life, sticky rice to keep the family close, and often twelve round fruits, one for each month. Many people wear polka dots, as the dots look like coins and should bring wealth. At midnight coins jingle in pockets, children jump as high as they can to grow taller, and bad luck is chased away with noise: torotot horns, banging pots, car horns. Firecrackers are allowed only at community displays permitted by local authorities, and the health ministry asks people to swap them for horns and light sticks.

In the capital region last year the biggest free countdowns took place at SM Mall of Asia in Pasay, in Bonifacio Global City in Taguig and on Ayala Avenue in Makati. At Mall of Asia, fireworks set to music lit up the sky at midnight.

traditions.title: Media Noche and 12 fruits
traditions.text: At midnight family and friends sit down to eat: pancit for a long life, sticky rice for a close family. Next to them, twelve round fruits, one for each month of the year.

traditions.title: Polka dots, coins and a jump
traditions.text: Wear something with polka dots: the dots look like coins and call in wealth. At midnight jingle the coins in your pocket and jump as high as you can; they say it makes you grow.

traditions.title: Noise instead of firecrackers
traditions.text: Noise at midnight chases bad luck away: torotot horns, banging pots, car horns. The health ministry advises horns and light sticks instead of firecrackers, and fireworks at community displays.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in the Philippines: Manila | Time2Fest
meta.description: The Philippines rings in 2027 with Media Noche: pancit, twelve round fruits, polka dots and torotot horns. Manila's midnight falls at 16:00 UTC.

BR@utc-0400.text:
Brazil welcomes the New Year — Réveillon — in white. The custom began with Candomblé followers who, in the 1970s, came to Copacabana beach in white with gifts for Iemanjá, the water goddess; since then white clothes and flowers set out to sea have spread across the country. At midnight people on the coast jump seven waves, making a wish on each.

Manaus, on the Rio Negro, greets the year an hour after Rio. The main party is the free Réveillon on Ponta Negra beach; at midnight low-noise fireworks go off at three places in the city so as not to frighten children, older people and animals, and swimming is not allowed that night.

traditions.title: White and lucky colours
traditions.text: Most people dress in white, as all over Brazil. Some choose yellow for money or red for love.

traditions.title: Ponta Negra
traditions.text: The main party is on Ponta Negra beach by the Rio Negro: free concerts from evening until dawn. Swimming is not allowed that night.

traditions.title: Low-noise fireworks
traditions.text: At midnight fireworks go off at three places in the city at once — low-noise, so as not to frighten children, older people, autistic people and animals.

CN.text:
In China, 1 January is Yuandan, the Gregorian New Year. It is a short break: in 2027 the holiday lasts three days, 1 to 3 January. The country's main celebration is the Spring Festival, the lunar New Year, which brings nine days off in 2027, from 5 to 13 February. On the evening of 31 December many people watch New Year galas: national and provincial TV channels air shows with a countdown to midnight. Hunan TV aired the first such concert in 2005.

Beijing greets the year with a bell: since 1982 the Yongle Bell, more than 600 years old, has been struck 108 times at midnight in the Dazhong Temple. Last year the countdown was also held, for the first time, on the Great Wall at Juyongguan. Both venues were invitation-only; everyone else watched live on TV and online. Fireworks are banned inside the Fifth Ring Road and, since 2022, across the whole city except approved displays.

traditions.title: Three days of Yuandan
traditions.text: In 2027 China's New Year holiday runs from 1 to 3 January. The long break comes later: the Spring Festival brings nine days off, 5 to 13 February.

traditions.title: New Year galas on TV
traditions.text: On the evening of 31 December national and provincial channels air New Year shows with a countdown to midnight. The tradition began in 2005 with a Hunan TV concert.

traditions.title: 108 bell strikes in Beijing
traditions.text: At midnight the Yongle Bell at the Dazhong Temple rings 108 times; last year the ceremony was shown live on TV and online. On the morning of 1 January people greet the first sunrise on the Great Wall.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in China: Beijing | Time2Fest
meta.description: China greets 2027 in Beijing as the 600-year-old Yongle Bell rings 108 times at Dazhong Temple and TV galas count down. Beijing's midnight comes at 16:00 UTC.

SG.text:
Singapore's calendar holds festivals of many cultures side by side: Chinese New Year, the Muslim Hari Raya, Hindu Deepavali and Christmas. 1 January is a single day off, while Chinese New Year gets two: 6 and 7 February in 2027. The night of 31 December is celebrated across the island, with fireworks and events at Marina Bay, Kallang, Sentosa and Clarke Quay, and the People's Association holds countdown parties in residential neighbourhoods. A New Year concert is broadcast live on TV.

The first Marina Bay countdown took place in 2005 and, according to URA, drew more than 160,000 people. To welcome 2026, the fireworks over the bay came in four parts, from 11pm according to URA, and police closed waterfronts as they filled up. For 2027 a 10.30pm start has been announced, along with the first live stream.

traditions.title: Countdown in your neighbourhood
traditions.text: No need to head downtown: the People's Association holds countdown parties in residential neighbourhoods across the island. Six neighbourhoods have been announced for 2027.

traditions.title: Fireworks over Marina Bay
traditions.text: The country's biggest fireworks are over Marina Bay; to welcome 2026 they came in four parts. Police close waterfronts once they fill up, so it's worth checking crowd levels on Crowd@MarinaBay.

traditions.title: Midnight on Sentosa's beaches
traditions.text: On Sentosa's Siloso Beach, 2026 was welcomed with a Mediacorp concert. For 2027, midnight fireworks have been announced on two beaches at once, Siloso and Palawan.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Singapore | Time2Fest
meta.description: Singapore greets 2027 with fireworks over Marina Bay, neighbourhood countdown parties and an announced first live stream. Midnight there is 16:00 UTC.

CA.text:
Canada sees in the New Year differently in each province, but a few customs are known across the country. In Quebec people watch Bye Bye on 31 December, the comedy review of the year that Radio-Canada has aired since 1968 and that ends with the countdown to midnight; last year more than four million viewers tuned in. On 1 January the Governor General and the provincial lieutenant governors hold levees, New Year receptions open to anyone, children included.

In Toronto the main party is on the shore of Lake Ontario, near the CN Tower. Last year people skated to a DJ and listened to a concert at Harbourfront Centre, and at midnight ten minutes of fireworks set to music lit up the lake. Subway and commuter trains ran free that night.

traditions.title: See in midnight at Niagara
traditions.text: Thousands see in the New Year in Niagara Falls, Ontario: at midnight fireworks burst over the illuminated falls.

traditions.title: Drop in at a levee
traditions.text: On 1 January the Governor General and the provincial lieutenant governors open their doors to all: shake hands and wish them a Happy New Year.

traditions.title: Take a polar bear dip
traditions.text: On 1 January hundreds of people in Oakville jump into icy Lake Ontario, often in costume, raising money for clean water in other countries.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Canada: Toronto | Time2Fest
meta.description: At midnight in Toronto, 05:00 UTC, Canada greets 2027 with fireworks set to music over Lake Ontario, while Quebec watches the Bye Bye comedy review.

GE.text:
Georgia sees in the New Year around a big family table with Georgian wine, and the night is unthinkable without gozinaki, walnuts fried in honey. After midnight everyone waits for the mekvle, the first guest of the year, who brings sweets and is believed to decide the family's luck for the whole year. Homes glow with a chichilaki, a little white tree shaved from dried hazel or walnut branches and burned before Epiphany on 19 January. Then on 14 January the party comes round again as Georgia marks the Old New Year.

In Tbilisi, First Republic Square was last season's festive heart for almost a month, with a New Year's Village and concerts. There is no single city fireworks show: at midnight people launch their own from their balconies and the sky lights up over the whole city.

traditions.title: Welcome the mekvle
traditions.text: The first guest to cross the threshold in the new year is the mekvle: they bring sweets and the hosts treat them in return. People say the year depends on them.

traditions.title: A white chichilaki tree
traditions.text: This tree of shaved dried hazel or walnut branches is hung with small fruits and burned before Epiphany on 19 January, taking last year's troubles with it.

traditions.title: Fireworks from Tbilisi balconies
traditions.text: The capital has no single city show: at midnight fireworks go up from balconies all over Tbilisi. By day, stroll the festive First Republic Square.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Georgia: Tbilisi | Time2Fest
meta.description: At midnight in Tbilisi, 20:00 UTC, Georgia meets 2027 with fireworks fired from balconies, gozinaki on the table and the mekvle, the lucky first guest.

MD.text:
Moldova welcomes the New Year twice. On the night of 1 January carolers go from house to house with Plugușorul, a rhymed wish chanted to cracking whips, bells and the buhai drum, while Malanca troupes act out comic sketches in bright costumes. In the morning children go sowing, tossing a handful of wheat or maize into each home for a good year. Then on the night of 14 January, the Old New Year, villages do it all again and the table is laid once more: cabbage rolls, cabbage pies and cozonac.

In Chișinău the big night happens on Great National Assembly Square, by the Christmas fair and the tree. Last year thousands danced the hora there to the Advahov brothers' folk orchestra, carols rang out before midnight, fireworks followed the countdown, and Zdob și Zdub played until almost 3 a.m.

traditions.title: Sowing on 1 January
traditions.text: In the morning children visit relatives and neighbours and toss a handful of wheat or maize into the house, wishing wealth and luck for the new year.

traditions.title: A second New Year on 14 January
traditions.text: On the night of 14 January the old-calendar New Year comes round: villagers go out with Plugușorul, mummers dance the Goat and the Bear, and cabbage rolls and cabbage pies fill the table.

traditions.title: Hora and fireworks downtown
traditions.text: In Chișinău, head to Great National Assembly Square: last year the concert began at 8 p.m., fireworks went up at midnight and the hora went on until almost 3 a.m.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Moldova: Chișinău | Time2Fest
meta.description: At midnight in Chișinău, 22:00 UTC, Moldova greets 2027 with hora dancing and fireworks on Great National Assembly Square, then children sow grain at dawn.

PK.text:
In Pakistan the loudest New Year celebrations are in the big cities: Lahore, Karachi and Islamabad. They hold musical nights and concerts, and fireworks go up in public places where families gather. The holiday can be quiet too: in Karachi, the press reported, people pray in mosques on the last day of the year, photograph the final sunset from rooftops and send friends and relatives messages asking for forgiveness.

At midnight in Karachi crowds gather on Sea View beach, dancing to drums and exchanging greetings. Last year the event at Governor House opened with a Quran recitation and national songs and ended with the longest fireworks display the city had seen. Aerial firing and fireworks outside permitted places were banned last year.

traditions.title: A concert in a big city
traditions.text: In Lahore, Karachi and Islamabad New Year's Eve means musical nights and concerts. Fireworks go up in public places where families gather.

traditions.title: Midnight at Sea View
traditions.text: Last year at midnight young people and families danced to drums on Sea View beach. Set off early: cars and motorbikes pour in, and police and Rangers step up checks.

traditions.title: Governor House celebration
traditions.text: Last year the Governor House celebration drew thousands and ended with the longest fireworks display the city had seen. Fireworks outside permitted places were banned last year.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Pakistan: Karachi | Time2Fest
meta.description: Karachi, Pakistan, meets 2027 at local midnight, 19:00 UTC, with crowds dancing to drums on Sea View beach and, last year, big fireworks over Governor House.

QA.text:
Qatar's biggest celebration is National Day on 18 December: cities are decked in white and maroon, and fireworks go up over the Corniche in Doha, Katara Cultural Village and Al Maha Island. New Year fireworks are a recent tradition here, and 31 December is not a public holiday: offices and shops keep normal hours. Still, in the evening the country gathers for the countdown, and in 2026 the state agency QNA called the New Year show the largest fireworks display in Qatar.

That show is on Lusail Boulevard, just north of Doha. To welcome 2026, over 250,000 people came: laser shows and music from 6 pm, then at midnight a thousand pyrodrones and fireworks above Al Saad Plaza. Entry was free but for families only. The programme for welcoming 2027 has not been announced yet.

traditions.title: Countdown on Lusail Boulevard
traditions.text: In 2026 laser shows and music ran there from 6 pm, and at midnight pyrodrones and fireworks took off. Take the metro: on New Year's Eve it ran late, until about 1–2 am.

traditions.title: Souq Waqif and Katara
traditions.text: In 2026 Souq Waqif had free street acts and live music. Katara Cultural Village offered performances, car parades and activities for children.

traditions.title: Dinner at a hotel or on a dhow
traditions.text: Hotels in West Bay, Lusail and The Pearl host paid dinners and galas, and some dhows leave the Corniche around 8 pm and return after midnight. Alcohol is served only in licensed hotel venues.

meta.title: New Year 2027: Doha, Qatar | Time2Fest
meta.description: Qatar counts down to 2027 on Lusail Boulevard near Doha, where pyrodrones and the country's largest fireworks lit up last year. Midnight in Doha is UTC+3.

TH.text:
Thailand has marked the New Year on 1 January since 1940, but the traditional and biggest new year here is Songkran in April. On New Year's Eve temples across the country hold «suat mon kham pi», chanting that carries people from the old year into the new. According to the Department of Religious Affairs, more than 12 million people joined in last year, at temples and online. On the morning of 1 January people offer alms to monks: rice, dried food and everyday necessities.

In Bangkok the biggest countdown is at the CentralWorld mall: according to the organisers, more than 350,000 people gathered there last year. At ICONSIAM last year fireworks over the Chao Phraya River went up together with a drone show. And at Wat Arun the bells ring at midnight.

traditions.title: Chanting across the year
traditions.text: On New Year's Eve temples across the country hold «suat mon kham pi»: people chant and meditate as the old year turns into the new. At Bangkok's Wat Arun the bells ring at midnight.

traditions.title: Morning alms for monks
traditions.text: On the morning of 1 January people offer monks rice, dried food and everyday necessities, for a blessing on themselves and their families. That day many visit temples and shrines to seek blessings for the year.

traditions.title: Countdown on the Chao Phraya
traditions.text: In Bangkok midnight is welcomed outside CentralWorld and on the banks of the Chao Phraya. Last year at ICONSIAM fireworks over the river went up together with a drone show.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Thailand: Bangkok | Time2Fest
meta.description: Thailand welcomes 2027 with temple chanting, bells at Wat Arun and a countdown at CentralWorld; at dawn, alms for monks. Midnight in Bangkok: 17:00 UTC.

VE.text:
Venezuela sees in the New Year with music: end-of-year songs play — “Cinco pa’ las 12” (“Five to twelve”) and “Año Nuevo, Vida Nueva” (“New Year, new life”) by Billo’s Caracas Boys — and at home people play the national anthem. At midnight they eat twelve grapes, making a wish with each, and wear yellow underwear for luck. The festive season means hallacas and pan de jamón, and 1 January is a day off.

In Caracas the cathedral bells ring twelve times at midnight, and the country’s main New Year concert takes place on Bolívar Square. Above the city rises the green Ávila mountain, with the round tower of the Hotel Humboldt on its summit, and in the centre stand the twin Parque Central towers.

traditions.title: Twelve grapes
traditions.text: At midnight, eat twelve grapes and make a wish with each — one for every month. For luck, wear yellow underwear.

traditions.title: Bells and the anthem
traditions.text: At midnight in Caracas the cathedral bells ring twelve times, and at home families play the national anthem.

traditions.title: A walk with a suitcase
traditions.text: Dreaming of travel? Right after the midnight toast, grab a suitcase and walk it around the block.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Venezuela: Caracas | Time2Fest
meta.description: At midnight in Caracas, 04:00 UTC, Venezuela greets 2027 with twelve grapes and end-of-year songs, while the cathedral bells ring twelve times over the city.

AE.text:
In the United Arab Emirates 1 January is a day off in both the public and private sectors. In 2027 it falls on a Friday, so the year starts with a three-day weekend, and the first working day is Monday 4 January. Every New Year's Eve fireworks go up from the Burj Khalifa in Dubai. Only to welcome 2018 were they replaced by a light and sound show, which entered Guinness World Records as the largest ever staged on a single building.

Dubai will greet 2027 in Downtown. On 31 December 2026 the programme starts at 7 pm, Cirque du Soleil performs for the first time at 11:25 pm, and from 11:59 pm the Burj Khalifa facade will count down the last sixty seconds of the year. At midnight fireworks, a drone show, the Dubai Fountain and projections light up together. Last year, the show's creators estimate, over 1.7 million people watched it live, and to welcome 2025 the city's transport carried 2.5 million passengers.

traditions.title: A three-day weekend
traditions.text: On 1 January both the public and private sectors in the Emirates have the day off. In 2027 it's a Friday, so work waits until Monday 4 January.

traditions.title: Free viewing areas Downtown
traditions.text: Public viewing areas in Downtown are free and first come, first served, with LED screens showing the show, and you can bring food and non-alcoholic drinks. Roads there are due to close from 4 pm, so take the metro: over 1.1 million passengers rode it to welcome 2025.

traditions.title: Midnight at the Burj Khalifa
traditions.text: As scheduled, from 11:59 pm the tower's facade counts down the last sixty seconds of 2026, and at midnight fireworks, drones, the Dubai Fountain and projections light up together. This time Cirque du Soleil artists join the countdown for the first time.

meta.title: New Year 2027: Dubai, United Arab Emirates | Time2Fest
meta.description: Dubai, United Arab Emirates, greets 2027 with fireworks, a drone show and Cirque du Soleil at the Burj Khalifa, free viewing Downtown. Midnight: 20:00 UTC.

AM.text:
In Armenia, New Year is the biggest family holiday, and it lasts a whole week: from 31 December to Christmas, which is celebrated here on 6 January. People bake New Year cookies and set a generous table, with anoushabour at its centre, a sweet grain pudding decorated with dried fruit, nuts and pomegranate. Children write letters to Dzmer Pap, Grandfather Winter, who brings presents on New Year’s night. From 1 January doors are open to everyone, and family and friends visit each other.

In Yerevan the country’s main tree shines on Republic Square from mid-December, with a market next door in Shahumyan Park. Last year 2,026 drones and fireworks lit up the square at midnight. Mount Ararat, Armenia’s symbol, rises above the city, though the mountain itself is in Turkey; Khor Virap monastery faces it right by the border, 30 km from Yerevan.

traditions.title: Anoushabour at the centre
traditions.text: Try anoushabour, a sweet grain pudding with dried fruit, nuts and pomegranate seeds. In Armenia it is the centrepiece of the New Year table.

traditions.title: A week of visits to Christmas
traditions.text: From 1 January until Christmas on 6 January, go visiting with gifts and wishes: Armenian homes keep their doors open to everyone.

traditions.title: Midnight on Republic Square
traditions.text: In Yerevan, come to the main tree on Republic Square: last year a concert played there from 11 pm, and at midnight 2,026 drones and fireworks took off.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Armenia: Yerevan | Time2Fest
meta.description: At midnight in Yerevan, 20:00 UTC, Armenia welcomes 2027: tree and fireworks on Republic Square, anoushabour on the table and visits until 6 January.

AR.text:
In Argentina the New Year arrives at the height of summer. People welcome it over a long dinner with family and friends: asado, vitel toné (cold veal in tuna sauce), and pan dulce and turrón for dessert. At midnight everyone wishes each other well and clinks glasses of cider or champagne, while some hurry through 12 grapes. Then the young go out until dawn, and many families head for the Atlantic coast. In La Plata giant dolls of the old year, made of wire and papier-mâché, are set alight at midnight.

In Buenos Aires, offices downtown have long showered the streets with scraps of paper at the end of the year, even though the city asks people to stop. Noisy fireworks were banned here last year, so the midnight toast is the main event. The Obelisco stands on Avenida 9 de Julio, and the pink Casa Rosada, the presidential palace, on Plaza de Mayo.

traditions.title: Cider and pan dulce
traditions.text: Have dinner with family and friends, then at midnight clink glasses of cider or champagne and move on to the sweets: pan dulce, turrón and nuts.

traditions.title: 12 grapes and white clothes
traditions.text: After midnight eat 12 grapes and make a wish on each. Wear white, and before the party sweep the house from the inside out to clear away the bad.

traditions.title: Burn the old year
traditions.text: In La Plata neighbours build figures up to 6 metres tall from wire, wood and papier-mâché, then burn them at midnight to start the year from zero.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Argentina: Buenos Aires | Time2Fest
meta.description: At midnight in Buenos Aires, 03:00 UTC, Argentina toasts 2027 with cider, pan dulce and 12 grapes on a summer night, while La Plata burns dolls of the old year.

CL.text:
Chile sees in the New Year at the height of summer, so many people celebrate on the beach. At the family dinner there are lentils for luck, at midnight twelve grapes, yellow underwear is a must, and anyone dreaming of travel walks around the block with a suitcase. Selling fireworks to individuals has been banned since 2000, so the fireworks here are official shows only. The biggest, 'Año Nuevo en el Mar' in Valparaíso, draws over a million spectators.

In Santiago the heart of the night is the Entel Tower on the Alameda. For the arrival of 2026 the party returned there after a seven-year break: at midnight a thousand drones and seven thousand fireworks rose into the sky. Above the city stand Gran Torre Santiago, the tallest building in South America, and the Andes to the east.

traditions.title: Lentils and twelve grapes
traditions.text: Have some lentils at dinner for prosperity, and at midnight eat twelve grapes: one, with a wish, for each month.

traditions.title: Yellow underwear, a suitcase
traditions.text: Wear yellow underwear for joy and money. Dreaming of travel? At midnight, walk around the block with a suitcase.

traditions.title: Fireworks by sea and tower
traditions.text: There are no private fireworks here, so go to an official show: in Valparaíso they rise from the sea, in Santiago by the Entel Tower.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Chile: Santiago | Time2Fest
meta.description: At midnight in Santiago, 03:00 UTC, Chile greets 2027 with grapes, yellow underwear and a suitcase walk, and the city with drones and fireworks at Entel Tower.

DO.text:
The Dominican Republic sees in the New Year with family, and many people from the capital head back to their home town for the night. The season's festive table brings roast pork, pasteles en hoja of plantain wrapped in plantain leaves, moro (rice with pigeon peas and coconut milk) and Russian salad, with ponche and rum. At midnight, the "cañonazo", everyone eats twelve grapes, one for each month, with a wish. Yellow underwear calls money, red calls love.

Santo Domingo is the city of the first cathedral in the Americas. Its big party is on the Malecón, the seafront Avenida George Washington, where Telemicro has thrown a free fiestón until morning for over thirty years. Last year, despite the rain, thousands danced merengue, bachata and salsa for twelve hours straight.

traditions.title: A bucket of water out the door
traditions.text: Before midnight the house is swept outward through the front door, and as the year turns a bucket of water goes into the street to carry the bad luck away.

traditions.title: A suitcase at the cañonazo
traditions.text: The moment the midnight cañonazo sounds, people step out with a suitcase, empty or packed, and walk it around the block so the new year brings travel.

traditions.title: Fiestón on the Malecón
traditions.text: In Santo Domingo, Avenida George Washington becomes an all-night free concert of merengue, bachata, salsa and urban music, broadcast live on TV.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in the Dominican Republic: Santo Domingo
meta.description: At midnight in Santo Domingo, 04:00 UTC, the Dominican Republic greets 2027 with an all-night fiestón on the Malecón, twelve grapes and a suitcase walk.

EG.text:
Egypt sees in the New Year over a festive dinner — with family at home or in a hotel restaurant — with music and fireworks over its landmarks. The most famous backdrop of the night is the Giza Pyramids just outside Cairo: at the start of 2025 fireworks burst over them at midnight, and in other years the pyramids and the Great Sphinx were lit up in many colours. A week later, on 7 January, the country marks Coptic Christmas, a national holiday.

In Cairo the heart of the night is the Nile. Hotels and floating restaurants line the Corniche from Cairo Tower, and as midnight nears people gather on the riverbanks and bridges to count down the last seconds together. On the boats there is live music, belly dancing and tanoura. At midnight fireworks rise over the city centre.

traditions.title: Dinner with family
traditions.text: In Egypt the night often starts at the table — with family at home or in a hotel restaurant — before heading out for music and fireworks.

traditions.title: A Nile cruise countdown
traditions.text: Board a Nile boat in Cairo: dinner, live music, belly dancing and tanoura, and at midnight a countdown right on the water.

traditions.title: Midnight on the Corniche
traditions.text: Head to the Nile bank or a bridge: last year a dense barrage of fireworks lit up central Cairo and the Corniche at midnight.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Egypt: Cairo | Time2Fest
meta.description: At midnight in Cairo, 22:00 UTC, Egypt greets 2027 with family dinners, Nile cruises with belly dancing and tanoura, and a countdown on the Corniche bridges.

ID.text:
In Indonesia, New Year's Eve is unthinkable without the terompet, horns sold right along the roadsides. With family and friends people hold a bakar-bakar: they grill chicken or corn, drink coffee and stay up late. Before the new year almost every family gathers for a shared meal: long noodles for a long life, a whole chicken for family unity, ketupat for forgiving one another. And 1 January is a national holiday.

In Jakarta the Sudirman and Thamrin avenues close to cars for the night, with stages along the route and the main one at the Bundaran HI roundabout. Last year the city's official programme had no fireworks, out of solidarity with flood victims in Sumatra; a drone show lit up the sky over Bundaran HI instead.

traditions.title: A terompet horn
traditions.text: In Indonesia the New Year's Eve party is hard to imagine without a terompet horn. Vendors sell them right along the roadsides.

traditions.title: The family meal
traditions.text: Before the new year the family sits down to a shared meal. Long noodles stand for a long life, a whole chicken for unity, ketupat for forgiving one another.

traditions.title: Car-free night in Jakarta
traditions.text: For years now the Sudirman and Thamrin avenues have closed to cars on New Year's Eve. Stages with concerts line the route, the main one at the Bundaran HI roundabout.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Indonesia: Jakarta | Time2Fest
meta.description: Indonesia greets 2027 in Jakarta: car-free Sudirman and Thamrin avenues, terompet horns, bakar-bakar grills and a family feast. Midnight there: 17:00 UTC.

IN.text:
In India, New Year's Eve blends modern parties with traditional festivities. It is loudest in the big cities: Mumbai, Delhi, Bengaluru, Chennai, Hyderabad, Kolkata, Pune and Kochi host parties and concerts. Kolkata celebrates on Park Street, Goa on its beaches and Manali at its winter festivals. The country is hugely diverse, so many people also welcome the year with prayers and rituals.

New Delhi celebrates in style too. Last New Year's Eve, the centre around Connaught Place was closed to cars from 7 pm, and visitors heading to India Gate, where big crowds were expected, were advised to take public transport. And on 1 January 2025, Delhiites filled temples and gurdwaras, including Gurdwara Bangla Sahib near Connaught Place.

traditions.title: A party in a big city
traditions.text: Mumbai, Delhi, Bengaluru, Kolkata and other big cities greet midnight with parties and concerts, and in Kolkata the main celebration is on Park Street.

traditions.title: Goa's beaches or Manali's hills
traditions.text: Goa is famous for its New Year beach parties, and Manali in the mountains for its winter festivals.

traditions.title: The first day at a temple
traditions.text: Many people begin the year with prayer. In Delhi on 1 January, people visit temples and gurdwaras such as Bangla Sahib, Rakab Ganj, Akshardham and Hanuman temples.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in India: New Delhi | Time2Fest
meta.description: India welcomes 2027 with parties and concerts in its big cities, crowds at India Gate in New Delhi and temple visits on 1 January. Midnight is 18:30 UTC.

KE.text:
Kenya sees in the New Year both in church and out on the streets. On the evening of 31 December places of worship fill up as people pray and give thanks for the year that is ending, and the next morning churches open again for thanksgiving services. Others count down the final seconds in the streets, at restaurants and at concerts. At midnight come joyful cries and applause, people dance, and fireworks rise over the big cities.

In Nairobi the heart of the night is the Kenyatta International Convention Centre (KICC) in the business district. Last year a crowd gathered beneath its tower to count down to midnight together, while fireworks burst over the centre, Westlands and residential estates. Car horns sounded across the city too.

traditions.title: A crossover service at church
traditions.text: On the evening of 31 December churches are full: people pray, give thanks for the passing year and cross into the new one together. On 1 January there’s a morning thanksgiving service.

traditions.title: Fireworks over the KICC tower
traditions.text: In Nairobi, count down beneath the KICC tower in the centre. For the start of 2025 the shows here and over Old Mutual Tower were free and lasted about 25 minutes.

traditions.title: Cheers, dancing and car horns
traditions.text: At midnight Kenyans greet the year with joyful cries and dancing. In Nairobi last year car horns joined in — add your voice to the noise.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Kenya: Nairobi | Time2Fest
meta.description: At midnight in Nairobi, 21:00 UTC, Kenya meets 2027 with crossover church services and joyful cheers, while crowds count down beneath the KICC tower.

KZ.text:
Kazakhstan sees in the New Year with customs that go back to Soviet times. Before midnight the president addresses the nation on TV, and at midnight the national anthem plays. It is above all a family holiday: people gather at a festive table at home first, then head out to the city celebrations. At the start of 2026 the New Year break lasted four days in a row, from 1 to 4 January.

In Almaty the heart of the night is Astana Square, which locals call Old Square. Last year a concert of Kazakh pop stars ran there from 6 pm to half past midnight, and the fireworks began at exactly midnight. Nearby, a New Year market served hot drinks and tornado potatoes, and by the Republic Palace there was a skating rink with a tree and Ayaz Ata.

traditions.title: President’s address and anthem
traditions.text: Before midnight the president greets the country, and at twelve sharp Kazakhstan’s anthem plays.

traditions.title: A festive table, a long break
traditions.text: First dinner with family at home, then a walk around the city. At the start of 2026 people had four days off, 1 to 4 January.

traditions.title: Fireworks on Astana Square
traditions.text: In Almaty, head to Old Square: last year a concert ran there until half past midnight, and the fireworks began at midnight.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Kazakhstan: Astana | Time2Fest
meta.description: At midnight in Astana, 19:00 UTC, Kazakhstan greets 2027 with the anthem after the president’s address, and Almaty with a concert and fireworks on Old Square.

LK.text:
Sri Lanka's traditional new year, Avurudda, comes in April at hours set by astrologers, with kiribath milk rice and sweets, while the night of 1 January is a modern city celebration. At midnight families head to the seafronts, and five-star hotels hold galas with a buffet, a live band or DJ and a toast. The biggest crowds gather in Colombo: last year the police drew up a special traffic and security plan for the city.

In Colombo midnight is welcomed on Galle Face Green, where families and street-food stalls fill the promenade. Last year fireworks lit up the sky over Galle Face Green, Port City and the illuminated Lotus Tower. Close to midnight tuk-tuks are hard to find, so agree on the fare first.

traditions.title: Midnight on Galle Face Green
traditions.text: Last year at midnight fireworks burst over the Galle Face Green promenade, Port City and the Lotus Tower. Come early: police expect crowds and heavy traffic in Fort, Pettah and Kollupitiya.

traditions.title: Street food by the ocean
traditions.text: On New Year's Eve families stroll along Galle Face Green while stalls sell street food. From there you can see the illuminated Lotus Tower above the skyline.

traditions.title: A hotel gala
traditions.text: Hotels along Galle Road and around the lake sell tickets to galas with a buffet, a live band or DJ and a midnight toast. The 2025 gala at Cinnamon Life was reported at about LKR 35,000 per person.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Sri Lanka: Colombo | Time2Fest
meta.description: In Colombo, Sri Lanka, 2027 arrives at 18:30 UTC. Families pack Galle Face Green for street food, hotels host galas, fireworks lit the Lotus Tower last year.

LV.text:
Latvians call the evening of 31 December Vecgada vakars, the evening of the old year. Grey peas with herring are a must: folk belief says they bring health and money, and the peas have to be finished before midnight or the year will be full of tears. People also pour their fortune, tipping molten metal into cold water and reading the year ahead in the odd shape it makes. Above all, don't fall asleep before twelve, or you'll sleep through the whole year.

In Riga the night belongs to the Old Town. Last year six squares rocked to DJs from 9 p.m. to 2 a.m., with projections glowing on the House of the Blackheads. Nearby, a plaque in the cobblestones marks where, as the story goes, the first decorated Christmas tree stood in 1510. Fireworks in Riga are allowed for just one hour, from 00:00 to 01:00.

traditions.title: Grey peas before midnight
traditions.text: Put grey peas and herring on the table for health and money. Finish them before twelve: folk belief says leftover peas mean a year of tears.

traditions.title: Pour your fortune
traditions.text: Melt a small piece of metal, pour it into cold water and study the shape: Latvians have long read the coming year in it.

traditions.title: Town Hall Square, Riga
traditions.text: Find the plaque in the cobblestones where the 1510 tree stood, by the House of the Blackheads. Last year DJs played here and in nearby squares until 2 a.m.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Latvia: Riga | Time2Fest
meta.description: At midnight in Riga, 22:00 UTC, Latvia greets 2027 with grey peas, molten-metal fortunes and DJs in Old Riga's squares by the House of the Blackheads.

MX.text:
Mexico sees in the New Year over a late family dinner: turkey or pork loin, or, depending on the region, tamales, pozole or bacalao. At midnight people eat a grape with each of the twelve chimes, making a wish every time, a custom that came from Spain. The colour of new underwear tells what you want from the year: red for love, yellow for money, green for health. Before midnight the house is swept out towards the door to chase away the bad, and in the first minutes of the year people run around the block with a suitcase to bring travel.

In Mexico City the main party is on Paseo de la Reforma at the Angel of Independence, a 36-metre column topped by a golden winged Victory. Last year DJs played there until 2 a.m., Mayor Clara Brugada led the countdown from the stage and, by the city's count, more than 250,000 people came. Cups of twelve grapes were sold right on the street for 30 pesos.

traditions.title: A grape for every chime
traditions.text: Have twelve grapes ready and at midnight eat one with each chime, making a wish for each month ahead.

traditions.title: Suitcase round the block
traditions.text: As soon as midnight strikes, grab a suitcase and walk round the block: the further you go, the further you’ll travel this year. Yellow underwear is for money.

traditions.title: Party at the Angel
traditions.text: In Mexico City head to Paseo de la Reforma: last year DJs played at the Angel of Independence from 6 p.m. to 2 a.m., with free entry.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Mexico: Mexico City | Time2Fest
meta.description: Mexico greets 2027 in Mexico City: twelve grapes on the chimes, a suitcase dash round the block and DJs by the Angel. Midnight is 00:00 local, 06:00 UTC.

MY.text:
In Malaysia, 1 January is a state holiday: a day off in most states, but not in Johor, Kedah, Kelantan, Perlis and Terengganu. The country's calendar brings together the festivals of different peoples and faiths: Chinese New Year, Hari Raya Aidilfitri and Deepavali are federal holidays, often celebrated by everyone together. New Year's Eve is marked with countdowns and fireworks in many cities, from Melaka and Ipoh to Kuching, while some welcome it in prayer: last year in Putrajaya, thousands joined religious programmes at Putra Mosque.

Last year Kuala Lumpur saw in midnight in three places: KLCC Park beneath the Petronas Towers, with fireworks and a tower light show; KL Tower, with fireworks; and Pavilion in Bukit Bintang, with a countdown festival, pyromusical fireworks and lasers. Above the city also rises Merdeka 118, the second-tallest building in the world.

traditions.title: Countdown in your own city
traditions.text: Countdowns with fireworks are not just for the capital: last year more than 40,000 people came out in Melaka and more than 30,000 in Ipoh, and Kuching's waterfront ended the night with fireworks.

traditions.title: A year that begins in prayer
traditions.text: Alongside the fireworks, people across the country also gather to pray: last year in Putrajaya, thousands welcomed the new year at religious programmes in Putra Mosque.

traditions.title: Beneath the Petronas Towers
traditions.text: KLCC Park is Kuala Lumpur's favourite spot for watching the midnight fireworks. Last year it hosted a free evening with Malaysian artists, fireworks and a light show on the towers.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Malaysia: Kuala Lumpur | Time2Fest
meta.description: Malaysia sees in 2027 in Kuala Lumpur: a countdown at KLCC Park under the Petronas Towers and fireworks from KL Tower. Midnight is 16:00 UTC, for all.

PY.text:
Paraguay sees in the New Year at the height of summer, so the festive dinner is often held outdoors. The extended family gathers, and each household brings a dish: meat, sopa paraguaya and chipa guazú made with Paraguayan cheese. There is cold sidra, wine and beer, and for dessert clericó, fruit in wine. Last year the country’s biggest party was in Encarnación on the Paraná River: at least 80,000 people were expected on San José beach, and the midnight fireworks lasted 20 minutes.

Asunción lies on the bank of the Paraguay River, and December days here average almost 33 °C. At night the López Palace, seat of the government, glows above the bay. In the city, fireworks may only be sold with a municipal permit, at Mercado 4 and on a few plazas.

traditions.title: Dinner under the stars
traditions.text: Gather the family outdoors: everyone brings a dish, and the table holds meat, sopa paraguaya and chipa guazú with Paraguayan cheese.

traditions.title: Cold clericó and sidra
traditions.text: Chill the clericó, fruit in wine, and the sidra: at midnight adults toast with champagne or sidra, and children with juice.

traditions.title: Fireworks on Encarnación’s beach
traditions.text: Last year almost a thousand tables stood on San José beach by the Paraná, bands played from 8 pm, and the midnight fireworks lasted 20 minutes.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Paraguay: Asunción | Time2Fest
meta.description: At midnight in Asunción, 03:00 UTC, Paraguay greets 2027 with an outdoor family dinner, cold clericó and sidra, while López Palace glows above the bay.

RS.text:
Serbia welcomes the New Year twice. First comes the night of 1 January: 1 and 2 January are days off, and presents for children come from Deda Mraz, Grandfather Frost, who since Yugoslav times has arrived at New Year rather than at Christmas. Christmas itself falls on 7 January, and on the night of 14 January the Julian calendar brings the Serbian New Year, with another countdown and fireworks, even though the day is a working one.

In Belgrade, New Year's Eve has drawn crowds to Republic Square, in front of the National Theatre, for decades. Last year a fifteen-minute fireworks show burst from the Kula Beograd tower over the Sava at midnight, while brass bands in Santa costumes paraded along Knez Mihailova Street.

traditions.title: Presents from Deda Mraz
traditions.text: Children wait for Deda Mraz on New Year's Eve: since Yugoslav times presents have come at New Year, while Christmas is kept separately on 7 January.

traditions.title: Fireworks over the Sava
traditions.text: At midnight, look to the sky over the Sava: for New Year 2026 the fireworks from the Kula Beograd tower lasted fifteen minutes and could be seen across New Belgrade.

traditions.title: One more New Year on 14 January
traditions.text: On the night of 14 January the celebration returns by the Julian calendar: in 2025 Belgrade had a concert on Republic Square and fireworks over the Sava at midnight.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Serbia: Belgrade | Time2Fest
meta.description: At midnight in Belgrade, 23:00 UTC, Serbia greets 2027 with fireworks over the Sava and gifts from Deda Mraz, then celebrates again on 14 January, old style.

VN.text:
In Vietnam, 1 January is a public holiday, but only for one day: the main celebration of the year is Tết, the lunar New Year, which in 2027 falls on 6 February. At Tết the whole family gathers, ancestors are honoured, red envelopes are handed out and people watch who is first to cross the threshold of the home. So young city dwellers say 1 January is “for myself” — trips, friends and the countdown — while Tết is for family. The largest cities, including Hanoi, Da Nang and Ho Chi Minh City, put on fireworks on New Year’s Eve.

Last year in Ho Chi Minh City the main countdown was on Nguyen Hue walking street: the stage ran from 19:00 to midnight, the centre was closed to cars, and at midnight fireworks lit up the Saigon River for fifteen minutes. Thousands of people had gathered on the riverside since early evening.

traditions.title: Tết comes first
traditions.text: In Vietnam 1 January is a single day off, while Tết, the lunar New Year, is the longest holiday of the year; in 2027 it falls on 6 February. At Tết families gather for meals, honour their ancestors and hand out red envelopes.

traditions.title: Countdown on Nguyen Hue
traditions.text: Last year Ho Chi Minh City’s main countdown was on Nguyen Hue walking street: a stage, bands and DJs, seven big screens. From 21:00 the central streets were closed to cars, so people walked to the stage.

traditions.title: Fireworks over the river
traditions.text: Last year, right at midnight, fireworks lit the sky over the Saigon River and the city centre for fifteen minutes. People claimed spots on the riverside from about seven in the evening.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Vietnam: Ho Chi Minh City | Time2Fest
meta.description: Ho Chi Minh City counts down on Nguyen Hue walking street and fireworks light the Saigon River at midnight. On 31 December, Vietnam welcomes 2027 at 17:00 UTC.

CW.text:
Curaçao sees off the old year to the roar of the pagara, long strings of firecrackers lit to chase away bad spirits. From 27 December there are free fireworks shows every night, and Dutch oliebollen join the festive table. Before midnight many families clean the house thoroughly, fumigate it with incense and pass burning incense around themselves, believing the herbs bring luck, love and prosperity.

Willemstad, whose historic centre has been on the UNESCO World Heritage List since 1997, is split by Sint Anna Bay into Punda and Otrobanda. The loudest pagara on 31 December goes off in Pietermaai, from early afternoon, with DJs and live bands. In the evening families bring chairs and food to Brionplein square, the crowd spills onto the Queen Emma pontoon bridge, and at midnight everyone hugs and wishes each other a happy new year.

traditions.title: A string of pagara
traditions.text: A long string of firecrackers is lit to chase away the bad spirits of the old year. The island's biggest pagara roars on 31 December in Willemstad's Pietermaai, from early afternoon into a street-wide party.

traditions.title: Incense before midnight
traditions.text: The house is cleaned and fumigated with incense, and just before midnight people pass burning incense around themselves for luck, love and prosperity in the new year.

traditions.title: Midnight on Brionplein
traditions.text: Grab a chair and some food and head to Brionplein in Otrobanda: bands, a blessing from the bishop and, at midnight, hugs with everyone around you and fireworks over the bay.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Curaçao: Willemstad | Time2Fest
meta.description: At midnight in Willemstad, 04:00 UTC, Curaçao greets 2027 with roaring pagara firecrackers in Pietermaai, incense for luck and hugs on Brionplein square.

NZ@utc+1345.text:
New Zealand is one of the first countries to welcome the New Year — in the middle of summer. For many New Zealanders it is holiday time: since the 1950s families have left town over Christmas and January for beaches and campsites, and the habit has become part of local culture. The country's loudest midnight is in Auckland, where fireworks pour from three levels of the Sky Tower for five minutes.

The Chatham Islands lie 800 km east of the South Island, and midnight comes here 45 minutes earlier than in the rest of the country. After a day at the horse races, islanders raise a glass with visitors, and Kahuitara Point on Pitt Island is the first inhabited place to see the year's first sunrise. The main settlement is Waitangi on the west coast, and basalt columns can be seen at Ohira Bay.

traditions.title: The year's first sunrise
traditions.text: Kahuitara Point on Pitt Island is the first inhabited place to see the new year's sunrise. In 2000 about 300 people greeted the dawn on Mt Rangaika with a haka and a blown conch.

traditions.title: Horse races
traditions.text: Around Christmas the island spends three days at the races: the local jockey club was founded in 1874 and is the second oldest in the country. Picnic blankets go down right in front of the trucks.

traditions.title: A toast before everyone
traditions.text: At midnight, 45 minutes before Auckland, islanders raise a glass, and visitors from the mainland celebrate with locals at the hotel in Waitangi.

AU@utc+1000.text:
Australia welcomes the New Year in midsummer, so the party moves outdoors: to beaches, parks, boats or a backyard barbecue. At midnight fireworks burst over the cities and glasses fill with champagne or wine. That night the country runs on several time zones: Queensland does not switch to daylight saving, so midnight arrives here an hour later than in Sydney. In the twin towns of Tweed Heads and Coolangatta, on the state border, crossing the street is enough to see the year in twice.

Brisbane, the capital of Queensland, celebrates over the river that shares its name. The council's free fireworks go up twice, at 7:45 pm for families and at midnight; in 2025 they were launched for the first time from four spots along the river at once, and ABC reported about 90,000 people at South Bank. The Story Bridge over the Brisbane River is the longest cantilever bridge in Australia.

traditions.title: Midnight twice in one night
traditions.text: In summer New South Wales is an hour ahead of Queensland. In Tweed Heads and Coolangatta the border runs along a street, so you can raise a glass twice: first on the southern side, then an hour later on the northern one.

traditions.title: An early show at 7:45 pm
traditions.text: For those who won't last until midnight, the first fireworks over the river go up at 7:45 pm. In 2025 two drone shows filled the gap, at 9 pm and 11 pm.

traditions.title: A cliff-top view, a free ride
traditions.text: Besides South Bank, the Kangaroo Point cliffs and the City Botanic Gardens give a good view. Getting home is free: in 2025 buses, trains and ferries carried everyone from 8 pm to 5:30 am, with CityCats every 15 minutes.

AU@utc+1030.text:
Australia sees in the New Year in midsummer, so the party moves outdoors: fireworks, concerts, parties on beaches and in city parks. Some gather friends for a barbecue or head out on a boat, and at midnight, under the fireworks, glasses of champagne or wine go up. 31 December is not a day off; 1 January is.

Adelaide, the capital of South Australia, welcomes the year half an hour after Sydney. The main party is free, in Elder Park on the bank of the Torrens: local musicians play from the evening, a family fireworks show goes up at 9 pm and the main one at midnight. Nearby, between the Torrens and North Adelaide, stands Adelaide Oval.

traditions.title: Summer, boats and barbecues
