traditions.text: At midnight the Cotai resorts have fired 8 minutes of fireworks. At Lunar New Year the fireworks rise opposite Macau Tower, watched from the shore of Nam Van Lake.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Macau | Time2Fest
meta.description: At 16:00 UTC Macau greets 2027 with countdown concerts by Sai Van Lake and in Taipa and Cotai resort fireworks, then a golden dragon parade in February.

NP.text:
Nepal's official calendar is Bikram Sambat, so the country's own New Year comes in April, on 1 Baisakh, when Bhaktapur fills with the nine-day Bisket Jatra. Late December is festive too. On 30 December the Gurungs celebrate Tamu Lhosar, their New Year, with feasts and cultural shows, and 1 January is National Costume and Hat Day, when young people put on daura suruwal, gunyu choli and the topi. Nepal reaches midnight on 1 January at 18:15 UTC.

In Kathmandu, New Year's Eve belongs to Thamel. The local tourism council holds a festival every year on the main street with music and cultural shows — in 2022 it ran until half past midnight, and about 180,000 people were expected to welcome 2024. Visitors also find events around the Boudhanath stupa, and hotels see the year in with live bands and banquets.

traditions.title: Thamel at midnight
traditions.text: On 31 December Thamel's main street turns into a festival of music and lights, packed with locals and travellers. The area's clubs and restaurants stay open well past midnight.

traditions.title: Tamu Lhosar on 30 December
traditions.text: The Gurungs see off one year of their twelve-year animal cycle and welcome the next. In Kathmandu the festival gathers people on the Tundikhel parade ground for cultural shows and feasting.

traditions.title: 1 January in a topi
traditions.text: The first day of the year is National Costume and Hat Day in Nepal. Young people dress in daura suruwal and gunyu choli, put on a topi and share photos.

meta.title: New Year in Nepal: Kathmandu | Time2Fest
meta.description: Nepal reaches 2027 at 18:15 UTC: in Kathmandu the night belongs to the Thamel street festival, while the Gurungs mark their own Tamu Lhosar the day before.

UZ.text:
In Uzbekistan New Year is one of the most beloved holidays, and preparations start a month ahead or even earlier. At home people put up a tree — the archa in Uzbek — and place gifts beneath it. The festive dastarkhan is laid as generously as possible: the richer the table, the luckier the year, people believe. At midnight the champagne is opened and everyone makes a wish. Children are greeted by Qorbobo in his chapan and his companion Qorqiz; legend says Qorbobo lives on the highest peak of the Chimgan range and arrives on a donkey.

In Tashkent last season the main celebrations took place on the square in front of the Alisher Navoi National Library, every day from 25 December to 10 January. Tashkent City, the parks and streets of every district had their own trees, fairs and concerts too.

traditions.title: An archa with gifts
traditions.text: The New Year tree, the archa, goes up in every home, and gifts for the family are placed beneath it in advance.

traditions.title: A generous dastarkhan
traditions.text: The table is laid so that food overflows: the richer the dastarkhan, the luckier the year. At midnight — champagne and a wish.

traditions.title: Qorbobo’s donkey for luck
traditions.text: Qorbobo and Qorqiz come out on central streets and squares. They say whoever rides Qorbobo’s donkey on New Year’s night stays lucky all year.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Uzbekistan: Tashkent | Time2Fest
meta.description: Midnight in Tashkent is 19:00 UTC: Uzbekistan greets 2027 with gifts under the archa, an overflowing dastarkhan, a champagne wish and Qorbobo on his donkey.

BD.text:
Bangladesh has its own New Year — Pohela Boishakh on 14 April, by the Bengali calendar; UNESCO listed its dawn procession in Dhaka as heritage of humanity in 2016. Still, the night before 1 January is far from quiet — people simply call it “31st night”. And on the morning of 1 January schoolchildren across the country get new free textbooks: the day is known as the Book Festival.

In Dhaka midnight arrives at 18:00 UTC. Every year the city police ban firecrackers, fireworks and fanush sky lanterns, and in various years have closed bars and barred open-air parties. Yet at midnight lights still flare from rooftops across the neighbourhoods — that is how the capital welcomed 2026 too.

traditions.title: “31st night”
traditions.text: That is what Bangladesh calls New Year’s Eve. In Dhaka people see it in with friends and family at home and in venues: in various years police have not allowed open-air events or DJ parties.

traditions.title: Lights from the rooftops
traditions.text: Firecrackers and fireworks are banned, and a noise fine can reach Tk 5,000. Yet at midnight lights still rise over Dhaka — from rooftops and courtyards.

traditions.title: Book Festival on 1 January
traditions.text: Schoolchildren start the year with a stack of new textbooks, handed out free by the state — about 300 million were printed for 2026.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Bangladesh: Dhaka | Time2Fest
meta.description: At midnight in Dhaka, 18:00 UTC, Bangladesh greets 2027 on “31st night”: lights from rooftops despite police bans, and new textbooks on 1 January.

BH.text:
In Bahrain 1 January is a public holiday, though the country also has its own New Year, the Islamic one: 1 Muharram, whose date shifts every year. New Year's Eve closes a winter season of celebrations that runs from 1 December and takes in National Day on 16–17 December. At midnight the kingdom welcomes the year at eight sites at once: fireworks climb 250–300 metres and the country's largest drone show, 2,500 drones, fills the sky.

In Manama the main spots are Bahrain Bay, the beach and the Four Seasons hotel, whose facade carries a 3D light show, the Bahrain World Trade Center and the waterfront between the Shaikh Hamad and Shaikh Isa bridges. People come early and take public transport. And if you'd rather sit down to dinner, a beach hotel gala runs until 2 a.m., with fireworks by the sea.

traditions.title: Fireworks and drones
traditions.text: At midnight the year arrives at eight sites across the country at once: fireworks reaching 250–300 metres and a ten-minute show by 2,500 drones over the bay.

traditions.title: A gala dinner by the sea
traditions.text: On 31 December a beach hotel hosts a gala dinner from 8 p.m. to 2 a.m., with fireworks right on the shore. Tables are booked in advance.

traditions.title: A season from December
traditions.text: From 1 December Bahrain runs a holiday season: events across the country and National Day on 16–17 December. And 1 January is a day off to rest after the night.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Bahrain: Manama | Time2Fest
meta.description: Bahrain welcomes 2027 at 21:00 UTC with fireworks at eight sites at once, a drone show over Manama's bay and beach hotel galas that run until 2 a.m.

CX.text:
Christmas Island was named on Christmas Day 1643, so December here is special: light displays, carols by candlelight, parties and a visit from Santa. The new year arrives at 17:00 UTC, an hour after Perth. Yet the island has more than one new year: its 1,692 residents include Chinese, Australian and Malay families, and the loudest festival is Chinese New Year. It is the only place in Australia with two public holidays for it: lion dances, lanterns, a steamboat dinner at the Poon Saan Club and fireworks.

Flying Fish Cove is the island's main settlement and only port. Its beach faces west, with barbecues and picnic tables, and its sunsets are among the best on the island. Red crabs are predicted to spawn on 2–3 January 2027, and the cove is one of the easiest places to watch it.

traditions.title: Carols by candlelight
traditions.text: The island was named on Christmas Day, so the holiday is extra special here: light displays, carols by candlelight, parties and a visit from Santa.

traditions.title: The year's last sunset
traditions.text: Flying Fish Cove beach faces west, so it has some of the best sunsets on the island — plus barbecues and picnic tables.

traditions.title: Crabs before dawn
traditions.text: More than 100 million red crabs live on the island. On 2–3 January 2027 they are predicted to release their eggs into the sea before dawn, and the cove is one of the best places to see it.

meta.title: New Year on Christmas Island: Flying Fish Cove | Time2Fest
meta.description: Christmas Island greets 2027 at 17:00 UTC, an hour after Perth. Expect carols by candlelight, sunset over the cove and red crabs spawning in early January.

ER.text:
In Eritrea New Year falls between two Christmases. 25 December is celebrated mostly by young people in towns, while the main Christmas comes on 7 January, by the church calendar: after a fast, families clean the house, slaughter a sheep, make coffee and greet their relatives. 1 January is a day off too. New Year's Eve is spent in bars, restaurants and busy public places, and it usually ends with fireworks. New Year's resolutions are rare here — elders simply wish for a prosperous, healthy and peaceful year.

In December the cafés on Asmara's Harnet Avenue glow with Christmas lights, and carols ring out from the Catholic cathedral. A New Year concert is held every 31 December: once in Bahti Meskerem Square, where thousands gathered, and in 2024 at Cinema Roma, with songs, dance and poetry.

traditions.title: Cafés and a concert
traditions.text: Eritreans spend New Year's Eve in bars, restaurants and busy public places. In Asmara a concert of songs, dance and poetry is held on 31 December.

traditions.title: Fireworks to end the night
traditions.text: New Year's Eve usually ends with fireworks. In Asmara they have been set off over Harnet Avenue, the city's main street.

traditions.title: Christmas on 7 January
traditions.text: A week after New Year comes the main Christmas, a public holiday. After the Tsome Tahsas fast, families slaughter a sheep, make coffee and visit relatives.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Eritrea: Asmara | Time2Fest
meta.description: Eritrea greets 2027 at 21:00 UTC: an evening in Asmara's cafés, a concert and fireworks, then a week later Christmas on 7 January with coffee and family.

ET.text:
Ethiopia has its own calendar and its own New Year — Enkutatash, on 11 September: since September 2026 the country has already been living in the year 2019. At Enkutatash girls go door to door with drums, singing the New Year song and handing out bouquets of yellow Adey Abeba daisies, while families come home from church to injera and doro wat. 1 January is an ordinary working day, and for Orthodox Christians it falls within the 43-day fast before Christmas, Genna, on 7 January.

So on the night of 1 January Addis Ababa celebrates mainly in its international hotels. In 2025 the Sheraton party ran from six in the evening to two in the morning, with concerts, a DJ and fireworks, and 3,000–4,000 guests were expected; elsewhere a jazz night had free entry. The big winter night is still ahead: on the eve of Genna, church services go on until three in the morning.

traditions.title: Genna, 7 January
traditions.text: Ethiopian Christmas is greeted in church: the night service runs from about six in the evening to three in the morning. Many make a pilgrimage to the rock-hewn churches of Lalibela.

traditions.title: Enkutatash in September
traditions.text: The Ethiopian New Year falls on 11 September: girls sing the New Year song from door to door and give yellow Adey Abeba daisies, and the family gathers over injera and doro wat.

traditions.title: A party at a hotel
traditions.text: On 31 December Addis Ababa's international hotels draw thousands of guests to concerts, a DJ and fireworks until two in the morning. Tickets get pricier every year, so buy early.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Ethiopia: Addis Ababa | Time2Fest
meta.description: Ethiopia meets 2027 at 21:00 UTC with hotel parties and fireworks in Addis Ababa, though its own year began in September at Enkutatash and Genna lies ahead.

IR.text:
Iran's main New Year is Nowruz: it arrives at the spring equinox, on 20 or 21 March, the first of Farvardin in the Iranian solar calendar. Families set the haft-sin table of seven things starting with the letter sin — sprouts, vinegar, apple, garlic, sumac — and on the thirteenth day of the year everyone heads out into nature. 1 January is not a public holiday.

Yet Tehran also greets this New Year, above all its Armenians and Assyrians, the country's Christian communities. From late December, Mirzaye Shirazi and Nejatollahi streets near the Armenian churches fill with shoppers: trees, fairy lights, Santa Claus dolls, pastries. On the night of 1 January church bells ring, and the Armenian holidays last until 13 January.

traditions.title: A tree from Mirzaye Shirazi
traditions.text: Shops near St. Sarkis Cathedral sell trees, fairy lights and Santa Claus dolls. Not only Christians buy them: more and more Tehran families celebrate at home.

traditions.title: Bells on New Year's night
traditions.text: On the night of 1 January church bells announce the new year. Armenians keep celebrating: 5 January is Christmas Eve and the Water Blessing, and the holidays run until 13 January.

traditions.title: A party at Ararat
traditions.text: The Armenian community's best-known New Year venue is the Ararat Sport and Culture Complex in Vanak: charity stalls with treats and crafts, and live Armenian music.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Iran: Tehran | Time2Fest
meta.description: Iran reaches 2027 at 20:30 UTC: in Tehran, trees from Mirzaye Shirazi Street and Armenian church bells, though the country's main feast is spring Nowruz.

KH.text:
In Cambodia, 1 January is a public holiday, but only for one day: the main New Year here is the Khmer one, Choul Chnam Thmey — three days in mid-April with pagoda visits and sand stupas. Still, the calendar New Year's Eve grows more popular every year: on 30–31 December 2024 the country welcomed 3.53 million tourists, almost all of them Cambodians. Most head for Phnom Penh, the Sihanoukville coast, Siem Reap, Battambang and Kampot.

In Phnom Penh the party gathers on the riverside in front of the Royal Palace. The welcome to 2025 started as early as 15:00: the “Celebrating Cambodia” parade with three thousand performers, traditional theatre giants and Ting Mong puppets, food from 25 provinces, a concert and fireworks at midnight. The next year fireworks were cancelled amid tension on the Thai border, and the city met 2026 on Chaktomuk Walk Street — with food, local products and dance.

traditions.title: New Year on the road
traditions.text: At the end of December Cambodians travel around their own country in huge numbers: almost 3.5 million domestic trips in the last two days of 2024. The favourites are Phnom Penh, the sea at Sihanoukville, Siem Reap by Angkor Wat, Battambang and Kampot.

traditions.title: The riverside by the palace
traditions.text: In Phnom Penh the countdown happens on the riverside in front of the Royal Palace: a parade with giants and Ting Mong puppets, a concert, food from every province. When there are no fireworks, as in 2026, people stroll Chaktomuk Walk Street.

traditions.title: Their own New Year in April
traditions.text: Choul Chnam Thmey, the Khmer New Year, lasts three days in mid-April. Families go to the pagodas, build sand stupas, wash Buddha statues and pour scented water over their elders.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Cambodia: Phnom Penh | Time2Fest
meta.description: Cambodia greets 2027 on the road and on the riverside by the Royal Palace in Phnom Penh: parade, concert, food from every province. Midnight: 17:00 UTC.

MN.text:
Mongolia began celebrating the New Year on 1 January in the socialist period, under Soviet influence. Today it is a day off and one of the biggest holidays of the year, and New Year’s Eve is mostly spent with family. Gifts for children and adults alike are brought by Övliin Övgön, Grandfather Winter, the Mongolian cousin of Ded Moroz. Don’t confuse it with Tsagaan Sar: the “White Moon” is a separate New Year, celebrated later by the lunar calendar.

Ulaanbaatar is the coldest capital in the world, so midnight here is usually bitterly frosty. Still, people gather on the central square by the 22-metre New Year tree for a concert, warm tents and hot food, and at the turn of the year a festive salute that has been a tradition for about a quarter of a century.

traditions.title: The tree and Grandfather Winter
traditions.text: The country’s main tree is the 22-metre one on Ulaanbaatar’s central square, and Övliin Övgön brings gifts to children and grown-ups alike.

traditions.title: Midnight on the central square
traditions.text: On 31 December the square hosts a concert, warm tents and hot food, with a salute as the year turns. Afterwards free buses take people home to the districts.

traditions.title: The year’s first sunrise
traditions.text: On the morning of 1 January people greet the first sunrise with offerings of milk and tea and wish for health and success, a good sign for the whole year.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Mongolia: Ulaanbaatar | Time2Fest
meta.description: At midnight in Ulaanbaatar, 16:00 UTC, Mongolia greets 2027 with a salute over the central square, a 22-metre tree and gifts from Grandfather Winter.

MU.text:
In Mauritius New Year is celebrated by every community on the island, so there are two days off: 1 and 2 January. The evening of 31 December belongs to the family, often around a barbecue. Many families pitch tents on beaches such as Albion from the 30th and cook a shared dinner right by the sea. At midnight firecrackers bang all over the island: the noise is said to chase away evil spirits. Even when they get pricier, people still buy them so as not to break the tradition.

In Port Louis midnight comes at 20:00 UTC. The best place to greet it is Fort Adelaide, the Citadel on a hill above the capital: from there you can see several fireworks displays over the city and its outskirts at once.

traditions.title: A night on the beach
traditions.text: At the end of December beaches become temporary villages: families pitch tents, bring pots and coolers full of food and sometimes stay together until sunrise.

traditions.title: Firecrackers at midnight
traditions.text: Firecrackers and fireworks are sold at markets, in supermarkets and by street vendors. At midnight they go off all over the island to chase away evil spirits.

traditions.title: A two-day holiday
traditions.text: 1 and 2 January are public holidays, so there is no rush. And Chinese New Year, the Spring Festival, is a public holiday in Mauritius too.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Mauritius: Port Louis | Time2Fest
meta.description: Mauritius greets 2027 at 20:00 UTC: family barbecues, tents on the beaches, firecrackers across the island at midnight and fireworks over Port Louis.

OM.text:
Oman has two New Years, but only one is a public holiday: the Islamic New Year, 1 Muharram, whose date shifts every year. 1 January is not on the list of holidays, so New Year's Eve here is calm: there is no city-wide countdown in the squares, and people see the year in mostly at hotels and restaurants, over a festive dinner with live music and a DJ until three in the morning.

The first day of the year, though, opens Muscat's winter festival: on 1 January 2026 the month-long Muscat Nights began in Qurum and Al Amerat parks, by the Royal Opera House and on Seeb Beach. Every evening brings a drone show, and the Heritage Village offers crafts, folk arts and Omani food. And on 11 January, Accession Day, fireworks rose over Seeb.

traditions.title: Dinner at a hotel
traditions.text: On 31 December Muscat's hotels host festive dinners: live bands, a DJ and dancing until three in the morning. Book a table in advance.

traditions.title: Muscat Nights
traditions.text: From 1 January, a month of festival in Muscat's parks: a drone show every evening, concerts and a Heritage Village with crafts and Omani dishes.

traditions.title: Fireworks on 11 January
traditions.text: Accession Day, marking the Sultan's accession to the throne, is a public holiday. In 2026 it was celebrated with fireworks in Seeb, on the coast of Muscat Governorate.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Oman: Muscat | Time2Fest
meta.description: Oman greets 2027 at 20:00 UTC: festive dinners in Muscat's hotels, then from 1 January the Muscat Nights festival with drone shows and a Heritage Village.

RE.text:
Réunion keeps UTC+4 all year, so midnight arrives here at 20:00 UTC. The New Year lands in the height of the southern summer, and the evening of 31 December brings family and friends together: first rhum arrangé or punch with samosas and bouchons, then prawn or duck curry and goat massalé, with lychees for dessert. On the west coast thousands pitch tents under the casuarina trees on the beaches of L’Ermitage and La Saline as early as 30 December, and at midnight they dive into the lagoon. On the stroke of twelve firecrackers go off across the whole island, said to chase away evil spirits.

In Saint-Denis people stock up on firecrackers early. Some see in the year at a picnic at Mamode-Camp in Le Brûlé, on the slopes above the city, while others head for the western beaches. In 2025 the island’s only municipal fireworks display was in Saint-Pierre, so midnight in the capital is mostly firecrackers set off in yards and streets.

traditions.title: Firecrackers at midnight
traditions.text: At exactly midnight the whole island bursts with firecrackers, and long strings of bangers are lit in front of houses: the noise is said to drive out the old year’s evil spirits.

traditions.title: A night under the filaos
traditions.text: From 30 December families pitch tents on the beaches of L’Ermitage and La Saline, fire up the grill and the music, and at midnight dive into the warm lagoon.

traditions.title: A slice of pâté créole
traditions.text: New Year means pâté créole, a pie filled with pork or chicken or a sweet one with jam, served with a small glass of anisette.

meta.title: New Year in Réunion: Saint-Denis | Time2Fest
meta.description: Réunion greets 2027 at 20:00 UTC. Firecrackers crackle across the island at midnight, and on the western beaches people camp in tents and dive into the lagoon.

SC.text:
In Seychelles New Year is louder than Christmas, and there are two days off: 1 and 2 January. On 31 December people give thanks for the passing year, and town fills with shoppers picking up food and new clothes: the year is greeted in everything new. In the past families slaughtered their own pig and shared the meat with neighbours, cooked stew and black pudding, roasted pork in the iron pot called a marmit, and after the feast went from house to house with good wishes. At midnight comes the countdown, champagne corks pop and the party lasts till morning; on 1 January many go to church.

In Victoria midnight comes at 20:00 UTC. The Mayor's festive programme runs all December along Independence Avenue, and on 31 December it ends with the Reveyon party at Stad Popiler: live bands, food stalls, a countdown on a big screen and dancing until 2 am.

traditions.title: Pork and coconut curry
traditions.text: The traditional festive table means pork in every form, black pudding and chicken curry with coconut milk, with homemade papaya and java-apple jams alongside.

traditions.title: From house to house
traditions.text: An old custom: go round neighbours and relatives wishing them a happy year, and in every house raise a small glass of lasante, to health.

traditions.title: Thanks and the first day
traditions.text: On 31 December people give thanks for the year gone by, and on 1 January they go to church. Some visit their loved ones' graves that day or the next.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Seychelles: Victoria | Time2Fest
meta.description: Seychelles greets 2027 at 20:00 UTC: new clothes, pork and coconut curry, New Year wishes from house to house and the Reveyon street party in Victoria.

SY.text:
In Syria 1 January is a public holiday, just like Christmas on 25 December and the Islamic New Year of the lunar calendar. So at the end of December the holidays follow one another: Christian neighbourhoods put up wreaths, red-and-white ornaments and festive markets, and men dressed as Santa Claus greet families right in the street.

In Damascus the Old City glows: fairy lights and Christmas trees in Bab Touma and on Straight Street, roasted chestnuts by the market. On the night into 2025 thousands saw in midnight under fireworks in Umayyad Square, and on the night into 2026, according to the SANA agency, people filled the Old City's streets again.

traditions.title: Old City lights
traditions.text: In Bab Touma and Bab Sharqi cafes, shops and balconies are hung with fairy lights, wreaths and Christmas trees, and small restaurants stay open late.

traditions.title: Roasted chestnuts
traditions.text: At the Christmas market in Old Damascus street vendors roast chestnuts, a warm snack for a cool December evening.

traditions.title: Midnight on Umayyad Square
traditions.text: Umayyad Square is where Damascenes gather on New Year's Eve: at the start of 2025 thousands came here and watched fireworks.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Syria: Damascus | Time2Fest
meta.description: Syria greets 2027 at 21:00 UTC: fairy lights and Christmas trees in Bab Touma, roasted chestnuts at the Old Damascus market and midnight on Umayyad Square.

TM.text:
Turkmenistan's own old new year comes in spring: Nowruz, on 21–22 March. Still, 1 January is a day off here too, so the night before is spent with family. The table is often laid right on the carpet over a large tablecloth. In the middle sits pilaf made with big, juicy elengi rice, next to Olivier salad, a holdover from Soviet times. Children write letters to Ayaz Baba in advance with their wishes. Midnight arrives here at 19:00 UTC.

In Ashgabat the country's main New Year tree is lit on 15 December in front of the Älem centre at the foot of the Kopetdag: in 2024 it reached 44 metres, with an eight-pointed star on top. Ayaz Baba and Garpamyk switch on the lights, and pines and cypresses along the streets glow with garlands. At midnight the anthem plays and fireworks burst over the city.

traditions.title: Pilaf on the festive cloth
traditions.text: The New Year table is often laid right on the carpet: pilaf with elengi rice in the middle, Olivier salad beside it.

traditions.title: The main tree at Älem
traditions.text: From mid-December the country's main tree glows in front of the Älem centre in Ashgabat, together with the trees on the squares of every province.

traditions.title: Anthem and fireworks at midnight
traditions.text: At midnight the national anthem sounds in Ashgabat, and then festive fireworks paint the sky over the city.

meta.title: New Year in Turkmenistan: Ashgabat | Time2Fest
meta.description: Turkmenistan welcomes 2027 at 19:00 UTC: Ashgabat's main tree glows by the Älem centre, fireworks burst at midnight, and pilaf waits on the carpet.

TR.text:
In Türkiye New Year is a secular holiday with no link to Christmas, and 1 January is a public holiday. Homes and streets are decked with lights, more and more families put up a New Year tree, and Noel Baba, the local Santa, comes for New Year itself. Most people see the year in at home with family and friends: the table is centred on a stuffed turkey with rice and chestnuts, with pumpkin and kaymak for dessert. In the evening the Milli Piyango New Year lottery is drawn: in 2026 the 800-million-lira jackpot was split by three winners. At midnight people wear something red for luck and break a pomegranate on the doorstep for a generous year.

Istanbul also takes the celebration outdoors: crowds fill Taksim Square, İstiklal Avenue and Kadıköy on the Asian shore. At midnight fireworks rise over the Bosphorus and the old city, and in Kadıköy in 2026 people counted down the last seconds with their phone lights.

traditions.title: Turkey with chestnuts
traditions.text: The star of the New Year table is turkey stuffed with spiced rice and chestnuts. After it comes kabak tatlısı, a pumpkin dessert with kaymak.

traditions.title: A pomegranate on the doorstep
traditions.text: At midnight, break a pomegranate on the threshold of your home to invite prosperity. And wear something red for luck.

traditions.title: Fireworks over the Bosphorus
traditions.text: At midnight fireworks rise over the Bosphorus. In 2026 crowds watched them at Ortaköy and at Sarayburnu point by the old city.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Türkiye: Istanbul | Time2Fest
meta.description: Türkiye greets 2027 at 21:00 UTC: turkey with chestnuts, a pomegranate broken on the doorstep, red for luck, and in Istanbul fireworks over the Bosphorus.

DJ.text:
Djibouti is a Muslim country with two New Years, and both are public holidays: the Islamic one, 1 Muharram, which shifts every year, and the civil one, 1 January. On the evening of 31 December the president traditionally addresses the nation with New Year wishes, and the city dresses up in lights: for the arrival of 2022, light displays lit up every roundabout and green space in the capital.

The main event of the night in Djibouti City is the city hall's free concert on the square in front of the Palais du Peuple. Thousands arrive in the evening, folk troupes and stars of Djiboutian song take turns until the twelfth stroke of midnight, and the party goes on late into the night. On 1 January the same square hosts the kermesse, a family fair, from the afternoon.

traditions.title: Concert at the Palais du Peuple
traditions.text: On New Year's night Djibouti's city hall holds a free concert in front of the Palais du Peuple: folk troupes, traditional dances and favourite songs until midnight and beyond.

traditions.title: Kermesse on 1 January
traditions.text: On the first day of the year a kermesse, a family fair, opens in the afternoon on the square in front of the Palais du Peuple. For New Year 2020 it was held for the fifth time.

traditions.title: A city of lights
traditions.text: For New Year the city hall decorates the capital: for 2022, light displays lit up every roundabout and green space, and a renovated garden opened on Place Lagarde.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Djibouti: Djibouti City | Time2Fest
meta.description: Djibouti greets 2027 at 21:00 UTC: a free city hall concert outside the Palais du Peuple, lit-up roundabouts in the capital and a family kermesse on 1 January.

BY.text:
In Belarus New Year is the main winter holiday: 1 and 2 January are days off, and midnight arrives at 21:00 UTC. It is welcomed at home around a festive table with Olivier salad, herring under a fur coat and tangerines, a custom kept since Soviet times. Presents for children come from Ded Moroz, Dzied Maroz in Belarusian, whose official residence is in the Białowieża Forest. The holiday sits between two Christmases, Catholic on 25 December and Orthodox on 7 January, both called Kalady here, when carollers go from house to house singing.

In Minsk the country's main New Year tree is lit in mid-December on October Square. On New Year's Eve festive venues open in every district of the city, and near the Palace of Sports the celebrations go on until four in the morning. For the night into 2025 the authorities planned no fireworks at the city events.

traditions.title: Olivier, “fur coat”, tangerines
traditions.text: A Belarusian New Year table rarely goes without Olivier salad, herring under a fur coat with beetroot, and tangerines.

traditions.title: Gifts from Dzied Maroz
traditions.text: Presents under the tree come from Dzied Maroz, the Belarusian Ded Moroz, whose official residence is in the Białowieża Forest.

traditions.title: Carols for Kalady
traditions.text: New Year falls between two Christmases, on 25 December and 7 January. At Kalady children and young people go from house to house singing carols and get small treats.

meta.title: New Year in Belarus: Minsk | Time2Fest
meta.description: Belarus greets 2027 at 21:00 UTC: the main tree glows on October Square in Minsk, and home tables fill with Olivier salad, herring and tangerines.

IQ.text:
Iraq has several New Years: the Islamic one, 1 Muharram, and spring Nowruz, celebrated mostly by Kurds. But 1 January is a public holiday too, and the night before it is loud in the country's cities: families and friends head out to squares and streets, trees and gardens glow with lights, children crowd around balloon sellers, and at midnight fireworks fill the sky.

In Baghdad many go down to the Tigris, to the Abu Nuwas corniche and Karrada: families sit right in the riverside gardens, music plays in the party halls and drums thunder. Others stroll Al-Rasheed and Al-Mutanabbi streets under winter lights. At the end of 2024 the city put up 14 decorated trees, the tallest, 30 metres high, in Al-Zawraa Park, where a concert went on all night.

traditions.title: An evening on the Tigris
traditions.text: In Baghdad families head to the Abu Nuwas corniche: they sit right in the gardens above the river, listen to the drums and wait for midnight.

traditions.title: Trees in lights
traditions.text: Streets and squares are hung with lights. At the end of 2024 Baghdad had 14 festive trees, the tallest, 30 metres, in Al-Zawraa Park.

traditions.title: Fireworks at midnight
traditions.text: At midnight fireworks fill the sky over Iraq's cities. They may be set off only in designated places, and celebratory gunfire is banned.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Iraq: Baghdad | Time2Fest
meta.description: Iraq greets 2027 at 21:00 UTC: fireworks over the Tigris, families in the gardens of Baghdad's Abu Nuwas corniche, trees in lights and an all-night concert.

JO.text:
In Jordan 1 January is a public holiday, just like Christmas and the Islamic New Year. Yet there is no shared countdown in city squares: people see the year in at hotels and restaurants, over a festive dinner with live music and a DJ, and some head to the sea, to the resorts of the Dead Sea or Aqaba. In the Christian town of Fuheis near Amman a huge Christmas tree is usually lit, and Muslims come for the holidays too. And in Petra, from Sunday to Thursday evenings, some two thousand candles light up the Siq gorge.

Amman greets the year with concerts: on New Year's Eve 2025 Nancy Ajram and Mohamed Hamaki sang in the capital's hotels, and at midnight the star of the night takes the stage. Abdali Boulevard closed at 8 pm on 31 December 2024, so the city celebrates at the table and begins 1 January with a leisurely brunch.

traditions.title: A concert at a hotel
traditions.text: On New Year's Eve stars of Arab pop sing in Amman's hotels, and the headliner takes the stage at midnight. Book a ticket with dinner in advance.

traditions.title: Petra by candlelight
traditions.text: From Sunday to Thursday evenings some two thousand candles light the Siq gorge all the way to the Treasury. 31 December 2026 is a Thursday.

traditions.title: New Year by the sea
traditions.text: Resorts on the Dead Sea, the lowest point on land, and hotels in Aqaba on the Red Sea hold New Year's Eve dinners with live music.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Jordan: Amman | Time2Fest
meta.description: Jordan greets 2027 at 21:00 UTC: Arab pop stars on stage in Amman's hotels, dinners by the Dead Sea and in Aqaba, and candles lining the Siq in Petra.

KG.text:
In Kyrgyzstan the traditional new year is Nooruz, a spring holiday on 21 March. Yet the night of 1 January is loved here too: it is a public holiday, celebrated with family around a big table. The main dish is beshbarmak made with horse meat or lamb, alongside manti, baked chicken and boorsoki, pieces of fried dough. Cooking is often done together, with old Soviet films playing in the background. The whole country reaches midnight at 18:00 UTC, and on 7 January Orthodox Christians mark Christmas.

In Bishkek the country's main New Year tree, 32 metres tall, glows on Ala-Too Square from mid-December, and nearby children get presents from Ayaz-Ata. On 31 December a concert starts there at 18:00, with an ice rink and a food court. The city fireworks have been cancelled two years running because of air pollution.

traditions.title: Beshbarmak on the festive table
traditions.text: Beshbarmak with horse meat or lamb is the main dish of New Year's Eve, served with manti and boorsoki.

traditions.title: The tree and Ayaz-Ata
traditions.text: From mid-December the country's 32-metre main tree glows on Ala-Too Square in Bishkek, and children collect presents at Ayaz-Ata's residence.

traditions.title: Concert and ice rink
traditions.text: On 31 December Ala-Too hosts a concert from 18:00, with an ice rink and a food court. Bishkek's mayor saw in 2025 here together with residents.

meta.title: New Year in Kyrgyzstan: Bishkek | Time2Fest
meta.description: Kyrgyzstan welcomes 2027 at 18:00 UTC: a 32-metre tree glows on Bishkek's Ala-Too Square, and family tables fill with beshbarmak, manti and boorsoki.

KM.text:
The Comoros has two New Years, and both are public holidays: 1 January and the Islamic New Year, 1 Muharram, whose date shifts every year. For many Comorians the end of December is a time to celebrate: on the 31st some go out to a restaurant, others head to the beach. The busiest is Mitsamiouli beach in the north of Grande Comore, where families, young people and their elders gather to sing and dance. For many it is a rare moment when the whole family is together, with adults off work and children out of school. The end of the year is also wedding season.

In Moroni people see the year in at hotels and restaurants over a festive dinner, with tables booked in advance; some celebrate 1 January at home with family. On New Year's night police patrols drive around the capital, keeping an eye on the roads and beaches.

traditions.title: To the beach as a family
traditions.text: On 31 December and 1 January Comorians head to the sea. Mitsamiouli beach draws the biggest crowd: families, young and old sing and dance.

traditions.title: Dinner at a restaurant
traditions.text: In Moroni New Year's Eve is spent at hotels and restaurants over a festive dinner. Book a table in advance.

traditions.title: Two New Years
traditions.text: 1 January is a public holiday. The Islamic New Year, 1 Muharram, is one too, but its date shifts every year with the lunar calendar.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in the Comoros: Moroni | Time2Fest
meta.description: The Comoros greets 2027 at 21:00 UTC: festive dinners in Moroni's restaurants, then families singing and dancing on Mitsamiouli beach on 31 Dec and 1 Jan.

KW.text:
In Kuwait 1 January is a day off: last year the government made Thursday, 1 January, a holiday, and state offices stayed closed until Sunday. The country also has its own New Year, the Islamic one on 1 Muharram, while its biggest celebrations are National Day and Liberation Day on 25–26 February. There are no mass midnight street parties with fireworks: fireworks need prior security approval, and last year the displays at shopping malls and on Messilah Beach were cancelled.

So the year is welcomed among your own people: at a hotel dinner in Kuwait City with live music until 1 a.m., at a mall, at a beach chalet or on a farm. And in winter many head to the desert: from mid-November to mid-March camps stand there, with coffee brewed over the fire.

traditions.title: A hotel dinner
traditions.text: On 31 December hotels in Kuwait City host dinners with a live band, a pianist or the oud, from 8 p.m. to 1 a.m.

traditions.title: A desert camp
traditions.text: From mid-November to mid-March Kuwaitis set up camps in the desert: coffee, a fire, traditional games and long talks into the night.

traditions.title: A long weekend
traditions.text: 1 January is a public holiday; last year, with the weekend, it made three days off. The biggest celebrations come later, on 25–26 February.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Kuwait: Kuwait City | Time2Fest
meta.description: Kuwait greets 2027 at 21:00 UTC with no city fireworks: hotel dinners with live music, nights at beach chalets and winter desert camps, and 1 January off.

MV.text:
The Maldives has two New Year holidays: 1 January and the Islamic New Year, 1 Muharram, whose date shifts every year. In this Muslim island nation the night before 1 January has no rowdy streets, but plenty of light over the water: resorts across the atolls hold their own fireworks and music nights. The sky has its say too: in 2023 the state night programme was postponed over a thunderstorm warning.

The capital sees the year in at Hulhumalé, a reclaimed island that is a district of Malé. For the past two years its Central Park has hosted a festival: Maldivian dishes from local stalls, boduberu drums, live bands. Before midnight a drone show rises, and at 19:00 UTC come the fireworks.

traditions.title: Festival in Hulhumalé
traditions.text: For a few days Central Park feeds and entertains everyone who comes: Maldivian dishes from local stalls, boduberu drums by day and live bands in the evening.

traditions.title: Drones, then fireworks
traditions.text: To welcome 2026, about 600 drones rose over the park, 75 of them carrying pyrotechnics. At midnight came five minutes of fireworks that draw people from all over Greater Malé.

traditions.title: Midnight on a resort island
traditions.text: Resorts across the country greet the year with their own fireworks and music over the lagoon. And 1 January is a public holiday, so there is no rush on the first day of the year.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in the Maldives: Malé | Time2Fest
meta.description: The Maldives greets 2027 at 19:00 UTC: a food festival and boduberu drums in Hulhumalé, a drone show, midnight fireworks and resort lights over the lagoon.

SO.text:
In Somalia, 1 January is a public holiday, as is the Islamic New Year, 1 Muharram. But there are no mass celebrations on New Year's Eve: in 2015 the Ministry of Religious Affairs banned public Christmas and New Year festivities as foreign to Islamic culture. The Somali New Year of its own, Dabshid, falls in July: young people jump over a bonfire to leap over the hardships of the year ahead, and in Afgooye people stage Istunka, a mock fight with sticks.

In Mogadishu the New Year is seen in at hotels: at the start of 2016, musicians played to a large crowd at one of the capital's best-known hotels. And on 16 July 2026 the city formally opened year 1117 of the Dabshid calendar.

traditions.title: An evening at a hotel
traditions.text: New Year's night in Mogadishu is spent at hotels: a concert, musicians and plenty of guests — that is how the year was greeted at the start of 2016.

traditions.title: A day off by the ocean
traditions.text: 1 January is a public holiday. Mogadishu's favourite place to unwind is Lido Beach in the north of the city, with its seafood restaurants and hotels.

traditions.title: The Dabshid bonfire
traditions.text: The Somali New Year comes in July: people light a bonfire of sticks and hay, and young people jump over the flames to leave the year's hardships behind.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Somalia: Mogadishu | Time2Fest
meta.description: Somalia meets 2027 at 21:00 UTC: a quiet 1 January holiday and hotel evenings in Mogadishu, while the Somali New Year, Dabshid, comes in July with bonfires.

TJ.text:
In Tajikistan the traditional new year is Navruz, a spring holiday in March. Still, 1 January is a public day off, and the night before is mostly spent at home with family and friends. The festive table mixes the familiar with the local: osh, the Tajik pilaf, with green tea, sambusa and qurutob, and for dessert baklava, halva and chak-chak. Children wait for Boboi Barfi, 'Grandfather Snow': they recite poems to him and get presents. The whole country reaches midnight at 19:00 UTC.

In Dushanbe the country's main New Year tree, about 30 metres tall, stands on Istiklol Square, surrounded by light arches, a house for Ded Moroz and a Ferris wheel. At midnight thousands gather around it, some from distant regions, a concert plays, and a big fireworks display crowns the night.

traditions.title: Osh and sambusa on the table
traditions.text: A New Year table in Tajikistan means osh with green tea, sambusa and qurutob, then baklava, halva and chak-chak for dessert.

traditions.title: Poems for Boboi Barfi
traditions.text: Children recite poems to Boboi Barfi, 'Grandfather Snow', and receive New Year presents from him in return.

traditions.title: Midnight on Istiklol Square
traditions.text: In Dushanbe thousands see in the New Year by the 30-metre tree on Istiklol Square: a concert, a fair and big fireworks at midnight.

meta.title: New Year in Tajikistan: Dushanbe | Time2Fest
meta.description: Tajikistan greets 2027 at 19:00 UTC: fireworks burst over the 30-metre tree on Istiklol Square, while homes wait for osh, sambusa and Boboi Barfi.

TZ.text:
In Tanzania, 1 January is a public holiday, and for many the night before it begins in church. On the evening of 31 December congregations across the country gather for New Year's services, giving thanks for the year that is ending and praying for peace and unity. Many hold a mkesha, an all-night vigil of songs and prayer that runs from nine in the evening until dawn. Others head to beach parties and clubs, while climbers set off for the summit of Kilimanjaro at midnight to greet the first sunrise of the year at 5,895 metres.

Dar es Salaam has no single city countdown: the city celebrates all along its coast. On the night into 2026, big crowds of all ages filled Coco Beach, and at midnight fireworks burst over the city, reflected in the Indian Ocean. St Joseph's Cathedral can be so full for the New Year's Mass that some people follow the service from outside.

traditions.title: Mkesha: a night in church
traditions.text: On the evening of 31 December churches hold New Year's thanksgiving services, and many congregations keep an all-night vigil of songs and prayer until five in the morning.

traditions.title: Midnight at Coco Beach
traditions.text: The busiest spot on New Year's Eve in Dar es Salaam is the public Coco Beach: families and groups of friends gather there, and at midnight fireworks light up the coast.

traditions.title: Sunrise on Kilimanjaro
traditions.text: Climbs of Africa's highest mountain, which also appears on the national coat of arms, are timed so that you set off at midnight and meet the year's first sunrise on Uhuru Peak.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Tanzania: Dar es Salaam | Time2Fest
meta.description: Tanzania meets 2027 at 21:00 UTC: all-night church vigils, crowds and fireworks on Coco Beach in Dar es Salaam, and the year's first sunrise on Kilimanjaro.

UG.text:
In Uganda, 1 January is a public holiday, and the festive season starts at Christmas: many city dwellers head to their home villages, and the big towns noticeably empty. New Year's Eve here is mostly a night of prayer — over 80 percent of Ugandans are Christian, and on 31 December churches hold overnight 'crossover' services to carry people into the new year. What began as small prayer meetings now draws tens of thousands. At midnight the fireworks go up: ahead of 2025, police approved some 2,900 applications from hotels, entertainment venues and churches, each display no longer than five minutes.

In Kampala, the 'Night of Prayer' in Naguru draws thousands of worshippers, and services fill the Lubaga and All Saints cathedrals too. At the royal Lubiri in Mengo, the Buganda Kingdom stages the Enkuuka festival, with concerts, tens of thousands of guests and the Kabaka, the king of Buganda, in attendance.

traditions.title: A crossover night service
traditions.text: On 31 December, join an overnight service: prayers and songs carry on to midnight, and the year turns in the middle of the service.

traditions.title: The Enkuuka festival
traditions.text: At the Lubiri in Mengo, the Buganda Kingdom sees out the year with the Enkuuka festival: a stage, musicians and tens of thousands of guests, with the Kabaka present.

traditions.title: Five minutes of fireworks
traditions.text: At midnight, fireworks from hotels, clubs and churches flare over Kampala — under police rules, each lasts no longer than five minutes.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Uganda: Kampala | Time2Fest
meta.description: Uganda greets 2027 at 21:00 UTC: overnight crossover services in Kampala's churches, the Enkuuka festival at the Lubiri and five-minute fireworks at midnight.

YT.text:
Mayotte keeps UTC+3, so midnight arrives here at 21:00 UTC. Most people on the island are Muslim, and the New Year is seen in with family on the shore of the lagoon, one of the largest in the world. The heart of the holiday is the voulé, a beach picnic: chicken, skewers, cassava, breadfruit and bananas go on the embers and the music goes on. In the old days people even pooled money for shared feasts at «bonne année». On 1 January the beaches in the south of the island fill up every year.

In Mamoudzou shoppers stock up on meat and drinks for the voulé before the holiday. Across the water on Petite-Terre, reached by ferry from the city, nearly a thousand people in home-made costumes join the carnival in Labattoir on 25 December. After Cyclone Chido in December 2024 the holiday was quiet, but the New Year’s Day picnics carried on.

traditions.title: A voulé on the shore
traditions.text: Gather family or friends on the beach, light the embers and grill chicken, skewers, cassava, breadfruit and bananas, with music playing.

traditions.title: New Year’s Day by the lagoon
traditions.text: On 1 January families head for the beaches in the south of the island, where rescuers keep watch and volunteers clean the shore.

traditions.title: Carnival in Labattoir
traditions.text: At the end of the year, on 25 December, nearly a thousand people parade through Labattoir on Petite-Terre with home-made costumes, decorated floats and their own songs.

meta.title: New Year in Mayotte: Mamoudzou | Time2Fest
meta.description: Mayotte greets 2027 at 21:00 UTC. On 1 January families from Mamoudzou and all over the island hold a voulé, a grill-and-music picnic on the lagoon beaches.

AX.text:
The Åland Islands are a Swedish-speaking autonomous region of Finland, so the New Year follows Finland-Swedish customs. Christmas belongs to the family, while New Year's Eve is a night for friends and guests. Finns have made New Year's resolutions since the 1880s, fireworks joined the celebration in the 20th century, and the oldest pastime is fortune-telling with molten tin. In the old days people also paid visits to friends on 1 January.

Mariehamn starts seeing the year out in daylight: on 31 December the town's New Year run sets off. At midnight the town fires its own display on the east side, between the library and the Alandica hall. In 2025 the council signed a multi-year deal: people want real fireworks rather than a laser show, and it means fewer private rockets.

traditions.title: Cast tin for luck
traditions.text: Molten tin is poured into cold water and the shape tells your fortune: a boat means a journey, a flower a wedding. Kits containing lead have been banned since 2018.

traditions.title: «Gott nytt år!» at midnight
traditions.text: New Year's Eve is spent with friends. As midnight strikes, everyone shouts «Gott nytt år!» — Happy New Year in Swedish — opens the champagne and clinks glasses.

traditions.title: The Nyårsruset run
traditions.text: At 12:30 on 31 December the New Year run sets off from the Mariebad pool in Mariehamn, over 7.4 or 9.5 km. Run or walk, prams and dogs welcome.

meta.title: New Year in the Åland Islands: Mariehamn | Time2Fest
meta.description: The Åland Islands greet 2027 at 22:00 UTC. Mariehamn fires its town display at midnight, after the Nyårsruset run on 31 December and an evening of tin casting.

BG.text:
In Bulgaria the star of the New Year table is banitsa with kasmetcheta, little pieces of luck: cornel twigs for health, coins and foil-wrapped wishes are hidden in the flaky pastry. It is cut in the first hours of the new year: the tray is turned three times and everyone takes the piece in front of them, and with it their fortune. On the morning of 1 January, St Basil's Day, the youngest in the family take a survachka, a cornel branch decked with ribbons, dried fruit and popcorn, and gently tap relatives on the back, wishing them good health.

Sofia welcomes the New Year in the open air on Knyaz Alexander I Square, where the concert starts at half past nine. At midnight the chant "Mnogaya leta" rings out, and then everyone joins hands for the horo. In recent years a light show has replaced the official fireworks, yet private fireworks still flash over the neighbourhoods.

traditions.title: Find your luck in the banitsa
traditions.text: Cornel twigs, coins and written wishes are baked into the banitsa. The tray is turned three times, and everyone takes the piece in front of them.

traditions.title: Survakane on 1 January
traditions.text: Children gently tap relatives on the back with a survachka, a decorated cornel branch, wishing them health, and get sweets or a few coins in return.

traditions.title: Horo at midnight
traditions.text: After the chant "Mnogaya leta", people join hands and start the horo, Bulgaria's best-loved chain dance.

meta.title: New Year in Bulgaria: Sofia | Time2Fest
meta.description: Bulgaria greets 2027 at 22:00 UTC: Sofia dances the horo on Knyaz Alexander I Square, and at home families seek their luck in the banitsa and tap backs.

BI.text:
1 January is a public holiday in Burundi, and New Year is celebrated across the country as a family day. Children visit their elders to hear their wishes for the year, and the feast moves from house to house so that no single family has to feed everyone. There is singing, dancing and drumming: the ritual dance of the royal drum has been on UNESCO's intangible heritage list since 2014 and is performed at feasts. People greet each other with "Umwaka mwiza" — "a beautiful year" in Kirundi.

In Bujumbura New Year's Eve is called "Bonane". On 31 December the streets around the Kuri Plaza market fill with discount stalls from the afternoon. At midnight some stand at services in packed churches, others in Independence Square, where on the night into 2026 a crowd saw in the year to DJ sets.

traditions.title: House-to-house feast
traditions.text: On 1 January children visit older relatives for their wishes for the year, and the meal moves from home to home, so nobody feeds everyone alone.

traditions.title: Midnight service
traditions.text: On New Year's Eve Bujumbura's churches are full: at prayer vigils the year is greeted with a countdown and prayers for a fresh start.

traditions.title: Independence Square
traditions.text: At midnight a crowd gathers in Bujumbura's central square: on the night into 2026 DJs played here, and the city greeted the year with a cry of "Bonane!".

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Burundi: Bujumbura | Time2Fest
meta.description: Burundi greets 2027 at 22:00 UTC: midnight services and DJs in Bujumbura's Independence Square, and across the country visits to elders and drums.

BW.text:
In Botswana both 1 and 2 January are public holidays, so for many people the season means heading home. Before Christmas town dwellers set off for their home villages, and families visit their cattleposts, the remote grazing grounds where the family herd is kept, slaughtering a goat or a cow for a generous meat feast. New Year's Eve services here are called 'crossover', a crossing into the new year: churches gather people from the evening of 31 December, and some congregations pray all night dressed in white.

Gaborone sees in midnight at parties and at festivals on farms around the city, while the National Stadium hosts a candlelit crossover every year. There is no single city fireworks show, but on the night into 2026 the Grand Palm resort threw a party with DJs and fireworks right at midnight.

traditions.title: Crossover in church
traditions.text: On the evening of 31 December churches call people to 'crossover' services, and some congregations meet the new year dressed in white, by candlelight, praying until morning.

traditions.title: Holidays in the home village
traditions.text: Before the holidays town dwellers travel to their home villages, and families head out to their cattleposts to slaughter a goat or a cow for a shared feast.

traditions.title: Midnight in Gaborone
traditions.text: The capital celebrates at parties and at festivals on farms around the city; on the night into 2026 the Grand Palm resort set off fireworks right at midnight.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Botswana: Gaborone | Time2Fest
meta.description: Botswana greets 2027 at 22:00 UTC: candlelit all-white crossover services, trips home to the villages and parties with fireworks at midnight in Gaborone.

MG.text:
In Madagascar 1 January is a public holiday, and New Year's Eve is above all a family night. Relatives gather at one home, often pooling money for the feast, and eat, sing and dance until midnight. The next day brings another meal: those who can afford it cook goose or turkey, and everyone exchanges wishes of "Arahaba tratry ny taona!". The Malagasy also have a New Year of their own, Alahamady Be: in March 2026 it was widely celebrated again with a sacred fire and tatao, rice cooked in milk with honey.

In Antananarivo some see in midnight at hotel parties and open-air dances, others at church. In recent years more and more people come at midnight to the illuminated square in Antaninarenina. And on the morning of 1 January the playgrounds of Anosy and Mahamasina fill with families in festive white T-shirts.

traditions.title: A feast everyone chips in for
traditions.text: The extended family gathers in one home and often pools money for the feast. On 1 January they lunch together; those who can afford it cook goose or turkey.

traditions.title: "Arahaba tratry ny taona!"
traditions.text: That is "Happy New Year!" in Malagasy. The first days of the year are a time to meet the family and wish each other a good year.

traditions.title: Another New Year in spring
traditions.text: The old Malagasy New Year, Alahamady Be, is celebrated again: in March 2026 with a sacred fire, a blessing and tatao, rice cooked in milk with honey.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Madagascar: Antananarivo | Time2Fest
meta.description: Madagascar greets 2027 at 21:00 UTC: family feasts everyone chips in for, wishes of "Arahaba tratry ny taona!" and the lit square of Antaninarenina.

SA.text:
Saudi Arabia has only four public holidays: the two Eids, Founding Day and National Day. Neither 1 January nor the Islamic New Year (1 Muharram) is a day off. A few years ago New Year's Eve passed quietly here; now the big cities greet it with a countdown and fireworks. In Jeddah people gather on the Corniche above the Red Sea, where the hotels along it host parties, rooftop countdowns and DJ sets late into the night.

In Riyadh, New Year's Eve falls during Riyadh Season, a ten-week winter festival of concerts, shows and sport. The main venue is Boulevard City, with live music and games for the whole family. The year 2026 arrived there with fireworks at the stroke of midnight, and pyrotechnics also lit up the Kingdom Centre and Al Faisaliah towers.

traditions.title: Fireworks at Boulevard City
traditions.text: Riyadh's main countdown is at Boulevard City: live music, games for the whole family and fireworks at the stroke of midnight.

traditions.title: Dinner above the city
traditions.text: Riyadh's restaurants and hotels host New Year's Eve dinners. In the glass globe atop Al Faisaliah Tower, dinner ran from 7 pm right up to midnight.

traditions.title: Jeddah Corniche
traditions.text: People gather on the Red Sea waterfront, and the hotels along it host parties, rooftop countdowns and DJ sets.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Saudi Arabia: Riyadh | Time2Fest
meta.description: Saudi Arabia greets 2027 at 21:00 UTC: a countdown and midnight fireworks at Riyadh's Boulevard City, and hotel parties along the Jeddah Corniche.

YE.text:
In Yemen 1 January is an ordinary working day. The public holiday goes to a different New Year — the Islamic one, 1 Muharram of the lunar calendar, which in 2026 fell on 16 June. The night of 1 January is not an official celebration: on 31 December the head of state sends New Year greetings to the leaders of other countries, as at the end of 2024. In Sanaa and other cities under Houthi control, New Year parties in hotels and cafes are banned, as the newspaper Asharq Al-Awsat reported in 2019.

Aden is called the “daughter of the sea”: water surrounds the city on almost every side. On holidays both locals and visitors from other provinces head to its beaches — Gold Mohur, Al-Arousa and the Khor al-Fil bay in Tawahi.

traditions.title: The Islamic New Year
traditions.text: The New Year that is a public holiday in Yemen follows the lunar calendar — 1 Muharram. In 2026 it fell on 16 June.

traditions.title: Bint al-sahn on the table
traditions.text: One of Yemen’s favourite dishes: paper-thin layers of dough with clarified butter. It is baked at home and served warm with honey and black cumin.

traditions.title: A holiday by the sea
traditions.text: Aden is surrounded by the sea on almost every side, so on holidays people head to the beaches of Gold Mohur, Al-Arousa or Khor al-Fil bay.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Yemen: Aden | Time2Fest
meta.description: Yemen reaches 2027 at 21:00 UTC: 1 January is a working day, the holiday is the Islamic New Year, and Aden, daughter of the sea, spends holidays at Gold Mohur.

CD.text:
In DR Congo, for many people the night into 1 January is the "night of the crossing": in churches they pray, sing and look back on the year, staying awake until morning. Others greet the year in bars, where bands and DJs play until dawn. Children look forward to new clothes and gifts, and families set money aside for a generous table and sweet drinks.

In Kinshasa churches pray from evening until dawn; in 2024 large services gathered on the esplanade of the Palais du Peuple and by the Échangeur tower in Limete. The real street party starts on the evening of 1 January: in communes such as Bandalungwa people put on their "New Year clothes", carry speakers out to the gate and dance. And in Matete the New Year is celebrated on 2 January, with a festival of its own.

traditions.title: Night of the crossing
traditions.text: On 31 December churches pray and sing from evening until morning, giving thanks for the year that is ending, and cross into the new one together.

traditions.title: New clothes, a full table
traditions.text: For the holidays children hope for new clothes and gifts, and families prepare a generous meal with sweet drinks.

traditions.title: Street party on 1 January
traditions.text: On the evening of 1 January people put on their New Year clothes, carry speakers to the gate and dance; Matete moves the party to 2 January.

meta.title: New Year in DR Congo: Kinshasa | Time2Fest
meta.description: DR Congo greets 2027 at 23:00 UTC: Kinshasa spends the night of the crossing in church, then dances in the streets in new clothes on the evening of 1 January.

CY.text:
In Cyprus the New Year belongs to Saint Basil. On New Year's Eve households once set a separate table for him with a candle, wine and the vasilopita, so the saint would bless the home. Today the cake with a hidden coin is cut at the family gathering: the head of the house crosses it and gives the first slices to Christ, Saint Basil and the home, and whoever finds the coin, the flouri, is the lucky one of the year. The first to cross the threshold should be a kind person or a child, right foot first, and a pomegranate is broken at the door for plenty and health.

Nicosia celebrates quietly: at city events drone shows have replaced loud fireworks, out of care for older people, babies and anyone frightened by bangs. And, as everywhere on the island, children go from house to house singing carols and receive sweets or a few coins.

traditions.title: Find the flouri in the vasilopita
traditions.text: The first slices of Saint Basil's cake go to Christ, the saint and the home. Whoever gets the coin is the lucky one of the year and keeps it as a charm.

traditions.title: Break a pomegranate at the door
traditions.text: The first to enter the house should be a kind person or a child, right foot first. A pomegranate broken at the door calls in plenty and health.

traditions.title: Carols from door to door
traditions.text: Children go from house to house singing New Year carols, and hosts thank them with sweets or a few coins.

meta.title: New Year in Cyprus: Nicosia | Time2Fest
meta.description: Cyprus greets 2027 at 22:00 UTC: Nicosia swaps fireworks for drone shows, and families cut the vasilopita with its lucky coin and break a pomegranate.

EE.text:
Estonians call the last evening of the year vana-aasta õhtu, the evening of the old year. Old belief says you should eat seven, nine or twelve times that night: each time you sit down to the table, you gain the strength of that many people for the year ahead. A little food is left on the plates for the ancestors and spirits said to visit that night. The table holds pork with sauerkraut, blood and white sausage, baked potatoes and swede, and for something sweet, gingerbread and marzipan.

In Tallinn the night draws people to Freedom Square: last year a free concert began at 10 p.m., and just before midnight everyone listened to the President’s New Year speech together. The city has skipped its own fireworks for several years, using flames, sparks and lasers timed to the music instead, though residents still light up the sky. On Town Hall Square stands a Christmas tree whose story Tallinn traces back to 1441.

traditions.title: Eat seven or nine times
traditions.text: Sit down to eat seven, nine or twelve times: folk belief says you’ll have the strength of that many people next year. Leave a little on the plate for the ancestors.

traditions.title: Sauerkraut and blood sausage
traditions.text: Serve pork with sauerkraut, blood sausage and baked potatoes with swede, then gingerbread and marzipan with your coffee.

traditions.title: Midnight in Freedom Square
traditions.text: Tallinn sees in midnight with a live concert in Freedom Square, where flames, sparks and lasers move to the music instead of a city fireworks show.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Estonia: Tallinn | Time2Fest
meta.description: At midnight in Tallinn, 22:00 UTC, Estonia greets 2027 with seven meals, sauerkraut and a Freedom Square concert of flames and lasers in place of fireworks.

FI.text:
In Finland, New Year's Eve is usually spent with family or friends. The late supper is simple and filling: sausages, potato salad and Jansson's temptation, a potato and sprat bake. The favourite fortune-telling game is tin casting: the metal is melted in a tiny ladle on the stove and splashed into a bucket of cold water, then the odd lump is turned by candlelight and its shadow is read. A ship, they say, means travel. Since lead was banned, the pieces are mostly lead-free tin, and nobody takes the predictions seriously anyway. From six in the evening until two at night, fireworks can be set off without prior notice, and the sky over the towns barely goes quiet.

Helsinki welcomes the year on Kansalaistori square by Oodi library. In the evening there is a family pyro show, at half past ten a concert begins that runs until the midnight fireworks, and the mayor gives the traditional New Year's speech.

traditions.title: Cast your tin
traditions.text: Melt lead-free tin in a ladle, splash it into cold water and read the lump's shadow by candlelight: a ship means travel.

traditions.title: Sausages and potato salad
traditions.text: The Finnish late New Year's supper is simple: sausages, potato salad and sometimes Jansson's temptation bake.

traditions.title: Fireworks from 18:00 to 02:00
traditions.text: On New Year's Eve, from 6 pm to 2 am, Finns set off their own fireworks without prior notice, unless the town has banned them in the centre.

meta.title: New Year in Finland: Helsinki | Time2Fest
meta.description: Finland greets 2027 at 22:00 UTC: Helsinki parties with a concert and fireworks on Kansalaistori, while at home families cast tin and read its shadow.

IL.text:
Israel's own New Year, Rosh Hashanah, falls in September or October, so the night before 1 January is known here as Silvester. It is not a public holiday: 1 January is an ordinary working day unless it falls on a weekend. Still, Tel Aviv makes it a loud night: restaurants serve festive menus, bars and clubs throw parties, and in Florentin and Jaffa people celebrate right in the street at midnight. Immigrants from the former Soviet Union mark Novy God in their own way, with a tree, Ded Moroz and a big family dinner.

Jerusalem greets the year more quietly, mostly at home. Before the holidays the city hands out about 350 trees at the Old City gates to Christians and immigrants from the former Soviet Union, and the Christian Quarter glows with festive lights.

traditions.title: Silvester in Tel Aviv
traditions.text: On the night before 1 January Tel Aviv's bars, clubs and restaurants hold parties and festive dinners, and in Florentin and Jaffa people celebrate midnight right in the street.

traditions.title: Novy God at the table
traditions.text: Families who came from the former Soviet Union lay a big table: festive salads, clementines, presents by the tree and Ded Moroz.

traditions.title: A tree from the Old City
traditions.text: The holiday tree is often bought from Christians in Jerusalem's Old City or in Jaffa, and every year Jerusalem's municipality gives out about 350 trees at the Old City gates.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Israel: Jerusalem | Time2Fest
meta.description: Israel welcomes 2027 at 22:00 UTC: Silvester parties in Tel Aviv, Novy God dinners with a tree and Ded Moroz, and free trees at Jerusalem's Old City gates.

LY.text:
In Libya, 1 January is an ordinary day: the public holidays include the Islamic New Year and Independence Day, so the end of December here is mostly about 24 December 1951, when the country became independent. Those who mark New Year's Eve do it quietly, at home with family, and its main sign is a festive cake. Libyans once even competed over whose New Year cake was decorated best and invited friends to house parties. And on 13 January the Amazigh towns take a day off to welcome their own New Year, Yennayer.

Tripoli has no city-wide countdown in its squares. In recent years the authorities of some districts of the capital, such as Abu Salim, have banned the sale of New Year decorations and sweets, and bakeries in the centre stopped taking cake orders on the eve of the holiday. So the capital usually sees the year in among close family and friends.

traditions.title: A New Year cake at home
traditions.text: The centrepiece of the night before 1 January is a festive cake, cut among family; people once even competed over whose was decorated best.

traditions.title: Independence Day, 24 December
traditions.text: The main state holiday of late December: Libya's independence was declared in Benghazi on 24 December 1951, and the day is a public holiday.

traditions.title: Yennayer on 13 January
traditions.text: The Amazigh New Year: in Amazigh-speaking towns, 13 January is an official day off.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Libya: Tripoli | Time2Fest
meta.description: Libya greets 2027 at 22:00 UTC quietly, at home with family and a festive cake. 1 January is not a holiday, and on 13 January Amazigh towns mark Yennayer.

MW.text:
In Malawi 1 January is a public holiday, and New Year's Eve here is above all a church night. Most people spend it at a crossover service, a crossing into the new year, while others gather for parties. The biggest services draw thousands: on the night into 2026 the crossover of the Enlightened Christian Gathering church drew about 17,000 people, including guests from more than 70 countries. Villages meanwhile celebrate mchezo with all kinds of dances, chiterera among them. At midnight shouts of joy ring out and some people set off fireworks.

In Blantyre the city council has already staged New Year fireworks: for the arrival of 2018 the show was held at the Old Town Hall on Victoria Avenue, with live music from Mingoli Band. That same night the Lilongwe council laid on fireworks and a concert too.

traditions.title: A night at crossover
traditions.text: On the evening of 31 December most Malawians go to church for a crossover service and meet the new year in prayer; the biggest services draw thousands.

traditions.title: Mchezo dances in the village
traditions.text: Villages celebrate the night with mchezo: people perform all kinds of dances, chiterera among them, and greet the year with shouts of joy at midnight.

traditions.title: Fireworks at the Town Hall
traditions.text: Blantyre city council has staged New Year fireworks at the Old Town Hall on Victoria Avenue; for the arrival of 2018 Mingoli Band also played live there.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Malawi: Blantyre | Time2Fest
meta.description: Malawi welcomes 2027 at 22:00 UTC with all-night crossover church services, village mchezo dances like chiterera and city council fireworks in Blantyre.

MZ.text:
In Mozambique, New Year's Eve is one of the best-loved celebrations of the year: houses are decorated with lights, people party in the streets, and fireworks go up at midnight. 1 January is a public holiday, and Christmas here is officially called Family Day, so the whole end of December is about big family gatherings. Many head for the ocean: in the 2025/26 festive season the country welcomed over 311,000 tourists and held 199 New Year events.

In Maputo it is the liveliest night of the year, with several fireworks displays over the city and parties in hotels and right in the streets. The city council allowed fireworks only from 23:50 to 00:10 and kept the beaches open until morning that night. Some years are quieter: on the night into 2025, fireworks were banned amid tension after the elections.

traditions.title: Family Day, 25 December
traditions.text: Christmas in Mozambique is officially Family Day: a holiday of music and big family gatherings, shared by Christians and people of other faiths alike.

traditions.title: Fireworks from 23:50 to 00:10
traditions.text: In Maputo the city council allowed fireworks only in these twenty minutes, so all the bangs land right on midnight.

traditions.title: A beach night till morning
traditions.text: On New Year's Eve Maputo's beaches stay open until morning instead of 20:00. On the sand, fish or chicken is grilled over charcoal and served with xima, a maize porridge.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Mozambique: Maputo | Time2Fest
meta.description: Mozambique sees in 2027 at 22:00 UTC: in Maputo fireworks fly only from 23:50 to 00:10, beaches stay open till dawn and fish sizzles over charcoal.

NA.text:
In Namibia the New Year falls in high summer: the holidays run from early December to mid-January, so many people head to the ocean or to family in the north, where about half the country lives. The night itself is often spent at a friend's home around a braai, meat on the fire, with dancing and food until midnight, while towns from Ondangwa to Okakarara hold countdown parties. On the coast Long Beach, between Walvis Bay and Swakopmund, fills with holidaymakers, and on the night into 2024 fireworks went up at midnight over Independence Beach in Walvis Bay.

In Windhoek the city council holds a free party every year by its head office on Independence Avenue: on the night into 2026 it was the All-White Party with local musicians. Only the city is licensed to set off fireworks, so at midnight they rise over the avenue.

traditions.title: A braai till midnight
traditions.text: New Year's Eve is often spent at a friend's home: meat goes on the fire, people dance and keep eating right up to midnight.

traditions.title: Summer by the ocean
traditions.text: The holidays fall in the summer break, so many head to the coast: on New Year's Eve Long Beach near Swakopmund is packed with holidaymakers.

traditions.title: Fireworks over the avenue
traditions.text: In Windhoek only the city council is licensed for fireworks: at midnight they light up Independence Avenue during the free city party.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Namibia: Windhoek | Time2Fest
meta.description: Namibia meets 2027 at 22:00 UTC in high summer: a braai with friends till midnight, busy coastal beaches and city fireworks over Independence Avenue, Windhoek.

PS.text:
In Palestine, 1 January is a public holiday, and winter brings several celebrations in a row: Christmas on 25 December, New Year and Orthodox Christmas on 7 January. Bethlehem marks them most visibly: a giant tree glows in Manger Square and scout bands with bagpipes parade through town. Because of the war in Gaza, the city cancelled its celebrations two years running; in December 2025 the tree was lit again, and thousands came to the square on Christmas Eve.

In Gaza, restaurants, hotels and cafés used to host private New Year's Eve parties. At the end of 2025, after the ceasefire of 10 October, a local artist sculpted "2026" in sand in Deir el-Balah, and the Holy Family Church lit its Christmas tree for the first time in two years.

traditions.title: The tree in Manger Square
traditions.text: Bethlehem's season opens with the lighting of a giant tree; on 6 December 2025 it was lit for the first time after two years without celebrations.

traditions.title: Scouts with bagpipes
traditions.text: On Christmas Eve, 24 December, scout bands with bagpipes parade across Manger Square, and on 6 January scouts welcome the patriarch there before Orthodox Christmas.

traditions.title: Days off on 1 and 7 January
traditions.text: New Year's Day is a public holiday, and a week later, on 7 January, Orthodox Christmas is a day off too.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Palestine: Gaza | Time2Fest
meta.description: Palestine greets 2027 at 22:00 UTC. 1 January is a public holiday, a giant tree glows in Bethlehem's Manger Square, and Orthodox Christmas follows on 7 January.

RW.text:
In Rwanda the New Year is celebrated more than Christmas, and both 1 and 2 January are public holidays. New Year's Eve is above all a church and family night: Catholic services start at 6 pm, Protestant ones at 10 pm, and afterwards people head to friends and relatives. On 1 January the family gathers for a festive meal and exchanges gifts. Among New Year songs the best loved is «Bonane» by Orchestre Impala.

Kigali's first fireworks went up in 2005 at Amahoro Stadium; today the main countdown is held at the Kigali Convention Centre. The city sets the fireworks for exactly midnight at several venues, and for the arrival of 2025 Musanze and Nyagatare put on displays for the first time too.

traditions.title: An evening service
traditions.text: On the evening of 31 December many Rwandans go to church: Catholic services begin at 6 pm, Protestant ones at 10 pm.

traditions.title: Midnight at the Convention Centre
traditions.text: Kigali's main countdown is at the Convention Centre; the city launches fireworks at exactly midnight there and at several other venues.

traditions.title: A family table on 1 January
traditions.text: On 1 January families gather for a festive meal and exchange gifts; visits can last longer, since 2 January is a holiday too.

meta.title: New Year 2027 in Rwanda: Kigali | Time2Fest
